nodes.statement_short: Projection functors commute with restriction to fibers

nodes.name: Fiberwise projections are O_z or 0
nodes.statement: Using this isomorphism for the sheaf~${\mathscr{F}}$ we started with, and taking into account Lemma~\ref{lemma:e-z-small}, we conclude that \begin{equation*} i_{Z_{d'} \times s}^*(\alpha_{d'S}({\mathscr{F}})) \cong \alpha_{d'}({\mathscr{F}}_s) \cong \alpha_{d'}({\mathscr{E}}_z) \cong \begin{cases} {\mathscr{O}}_z, & \text{if $d' = d$},\\ 0, & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Fiberwise projections are O_z or 0

nodes.name: Other projections vanish; F = Phi(F_d)
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise}$(i)$ it follows that $\alpha_{d'S}({\mathscr{F}}) = 0$ when $d' \ne d$, hence \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{F}} \cong \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d} \boxtimes {\mathscr{O}}_S}({\mathscr{F}}_d) \end{equation*} for some object ${\mathscr{F}}_d \in {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d \times S)$.
nodes.statement_short: Other projections vanish; F = Phi(F_d)

nodes.name: F_d is a line bundle on a graph by Lemma 4.4(iii)
nodes.statement: Moreover, the object ${\mathscr{F}}_d$ is such that for any geometric point~$s \in S$ we have $i_{Z_d \times s}^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_z$ for some closed point~$z \in Z_d$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise}$(iii)$ it follows that ${\mathscr{F}}_d \cong \Gamma_{f_d*}{\mathscr{L}}$, where $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$ is a morphism, $\Gamma_{f_d} \colon S \to Z_d \times S$ is its graph, and ${\mathscr{L}}$ is a line bundle on $S$.
nodes.statement_short: F_d is a line bundle on a graph by Lemma 4.4(iii)

nodes.name: Moduli functor represented by Z_d with universal sheaf
nodes.statement: Therefore \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{F}} \cong \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d} \boxtimes {\mathscr{O}}_S}(\Gamma_{f_d*}{\mathscr{L}}) \cong (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d} \otimes p_S^*{\mathscr{L}}. \end{equation*} This precisely means that the moduli functor ${\mathscr{M}}_d(X)$ we are interested in is represented by the scheme~$Z_d$, and that ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$ is a universal sheaf.
nodes.statement_short: Moduli functor represented by Z_d with universal sheaf

nodes.name: Dual decomposition gives M_4 and second family for M_3
nodes.statement: This proves the statement about~${\mathscr{M}}_2(X)$ and the first statement about~${\mathscr{M}}_3(X)$. The same argument applied to the dual semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbx-dual} instead of~\eqref{eq:dbx-dz} proves the statement about~${\mathscr{M}}_4(X)$ and the second statement about~${\mathscr{M}}_3(X)$.
nodes.statement_short: Dual decomposition gives M_4 and second family for M_3

nodes.name: Automorphism $\sigma$ of $\mathscr{M}_3(X)$
nodes.statement: There is an automorphism $\sigma \colon {\mathscr{M}}_3(X) \to {\mathscr{M}}_3(X)$ such that ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}^\vee \cong \sigma^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3} \otimes \omega_X$.
nodes.statement_short: The two universal families on $\mathscr{M}_3(X)$ differ by an automorphism $\sigma$.
conclusions: There is an automorphism $\sigma \colon {\mathscr{M}}_3(X) \to {\mathscr{M}}_3(X)$ such that ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}^\vee \cong \sigma^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3} \otimes \omega_X$.
nodes.label: corollary:tau-m3x

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 4.6
nodes.statement: Both ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}$ and ${\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ are universal families on ${\mathscr{M}}_3(X) \times X$, hence they differ only by an automorphism of ${\mathscr{M}}_3(X)$ and a twist by a line bundle on it. But since ${\mathscr{M}}_3(X)$ is zero-dimensional, it has no non-trivial line bundles.
nodes.statement_short: Two universal families differ by an automorphism and a line bundle; a zero-dimensional scheme has no nontrivial line bundles.

nodes.name: Polynomials $h'_d(t)$
nodes.statement: h'_d(t) = dt + 1 \in {\mathbb{Z}}[t].
nodes.label: eq:hdprime

nodes.name: Subschemes with Hilbert polynomial dt+1 are ACM curves
nodes.statement: Let $C \subset X \subset {\mathbb{P}}^6$ be a subscheme with Hilbert polynomial $h_C(t) = h'_d(t)$ and $1 \le d \le 3$. Then $C$ is a connected arithmetically Cohen--Macaulay curve.
nodes.statement_short: Subschemes of X with Hilbert polynomial dt+1, d <= 3, are connected arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curves.
assumptions: Let $C \subset X \subset {\mathbb{P}}^6$ be a subscheme with Hilbert polynomial $h_C(t) = h'_d(t)$ and $1 \le d \le 3$.
conclusions: Then $C$ is a connected arithmetically Cohen--Macaulay curve.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.7
nodes.statement: In cases $d = 1$ and $d = 2$ this is standard (see, e.g., \cite[Lemma~2.1.1]{kuznetsov2016hilbert}). In case $d = 3$ the only other possibility for $C$ (see~\cite[\S1]{lehn2015twisted} and references therein) would be a union of a plane cubic curve with a point (possibly embedded). But~$X$ is an intersection of quadrics by~\cite[Theorem~4.4]{hidaka1981normal} and contains no planes, so this is impossible.
nodes.statement_short: Standard for d = 1, 2; for d = 3 the only alternative is a plane cubic plus a point, excluded since X is cut out by quadrics and contains no planes.

nodes.name: Cases d = 1, 2 (cited)
nodes.statement: In cases $d = 1$ and $d = 2$ this is standard (see, e.g., \cite[Lemma~2.1.1]{kuznetsov2016hilbert}).
nodes.statement_short: Cases d = 1, 2 (cited)

nodes.name: Case d = 3: exclude plane cubic plus point
nodes.statement: In case $d = 3$ the only other possibility for $C$ (see~\cite[\S1]{lehn2015twisted} and references therein) would be a union of a plane cubic curve with a point (possibly embedded). But~$X$ is an intersection of quadrics by~\cite[Theorem~4.4]{hidaka1981normal} and contains no planes, so this is impossible.
nodes.statement_short: Case d = 3: exclude plane cubic plus point

nodes.name: Ideal sheaves of conics, cubics and lines
nodes.statement: $(i)$ If $C \subset X$ is a curve with Hilbert polynomial $h'_d(t)$ with $d \in \{2,3\}$ then there is a unique closed point $z \in Z_d$ and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{E}}_z^\vee \to {\mathscr{O}}_X \to {\mathscr{O}}_C \to 0. \end{equation*} Conversely, any nonzero morphism ${\mathscr{E}}_z^\vee \to {\mathscr{O}}_X$ is injective with cokernel isomorphic to ${\mathscr{O}}_C$. $(ii)$ Similarly, if $L \subset X$ is a line, i.e., a curve with Hilbert polynomial $h'_1(t)$ then there are unique closed points $z_2 \in Z_2$ and $z_3 \in Z_3$ and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{E}}_{z_2} \to {\mathscr{E}}_{z_3} \to {\mathscr{O}}_L \to 0. \end{equation*} Conversely, any nonzero morphism ${\mathscr{E}}_{z_2} \to {\mathscr{E}}_{z_3}$ is injective with cokernel isomorphic to ${\mathscr{O}}_L$.
nodes.statement_short: Conics and twisted cubics C have $I_C\cong\mathscr{E}_z^\vee$; lines L are cokernels of $\mathscr{E}_{z_2}\to\mathscr{E}_{z_3}$; conversely every nonzero such map gives a curve.
conclusions: If $C \subset X$ is a curve with Hilbert polynomial $h'_d(t)$ with $d \in \{2,3\}$ then there is a unique closed point $z \in Z_d$ and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{E}}_z^\vee \to {\mathscr{O}}_X \to {\mathscr{O}}_C \to 0. \end{equation*} Conversely, any nonzero morphism ${\mathscr{E}}_z^\vee \to {\mathscr{O}}_X$ is injective with cokernel isomorphic to ${\mathscr{O}}_C$.

Similarly, if $L \subset X$ is a line, i.e., a curve with Hilbert polynomial $h'_1(t)$ then there are unique closed points $z_2 \in Z_2$ and $z_3 \in Z_3$ and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{E}}_{z_2} \to {\mathscr{E}}_{z_3} \to {\mathscr{O}}_L \to 0. \end{equation*} Conversely, any nonzero morphism ${\mathscr{E}}_{z_2} \to {\mathscr{E}}_{z_3}$ is injective with cokernel isomorphic to ${\mathscr{O}}_L$.
nodes.label: lemma:oc-decomposition

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.8
nodes.statement: For the first part of~$(i)$, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-points}$(ii)$ it is enough to show that $I_C \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ is stable with Hilbert polynomial~$h_{6-d}(t)$. Stability is clear by Lemma~\ref{lemma:hd-stable}, and the Hilbert polynomial evidently equals \begin{equation*} h_{{\mathscr{O}}_X}(t+1) - h'_d(t+1) = (3(t+1)(t+2) + 1) - (d(t+1) + 1) = (3t + 6 - d)(t + 1) = h_{6-d}(t). \end{equation*} For the first part of~$(ii)$ first note that by Serre duality \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{O}}_L,{\mathscr{O}}_X) \cong \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{O}}_X,{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X))^\vee = H^\bullet(L,{\mathscr{O}}_L(-1)) = 0 \end{equation*} since $L \cong {\mathbb{P}}^1$ and $L \cdot K_X = -1$. Thus by Theorem~\ref{theorem:dbx} the structure sheaf ${\mathscr{O}}_L$ is contained in the subcategory~$\langle {\mathcal{A}}_2, {\mathcal{A}}_3 \rangle$ of ${\mathbf{D}}(X)$. Next, again by Serre duality \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^i({\mathscr{O}}_L,{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}) \cong \mathrm{Ext}^{2-i}({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2},{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X))^\vee. \end{equation*} Since ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}$ is a vector bundle and $L$ is a curve, the right hand side is zero unless $i \in \{1, 2\}$. On the other hand, ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}$ is globally generated by Proposition~\ref{proposition:e-z-big} and~\eqref{eq:cezd}, while ${\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_L(-1)$ has no global sections, hence for $i = 2$ the right hand side is also zero. On the other hand, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:chi-ez-f} we have \begin{equation*} \chi({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2},{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X)) = 2\chi(X,{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X)) + \chi(X,{\mathscr{O}}_L(2K_X)) - 3r({\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X)) = 2 \cdot h'_1(-1) + h'_1(-2) = -1, \end{equation*} and we conclude that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{O}}_L, {\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}) = {\mathsf{k}}[-1]$. This means that there is a unique closed point $z_2 \in Z_2$ and a unique extension \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{E}}_{z_2} \to {\mathscr{F}} \to {\mathscr{O}}_L \to 0 \end{equation*} such that ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathcal{A}}_3$. It remains to note that ${\mathscr{F}}$ is a sheaf of rank 1, hence there is a unique $z_3 \in Z_3$ such that ${\mathscr{F}} \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{z_3}$. The converse statements are evident.
nodes.statement_short: For (i) the twisted ideal is stable with polynomial h_{6-d}, so Lemma 4.3(ii) applies. For (ii), Serre duality and Lemma 3.20 show Ext(O_L, E_{Z_2}) = k[-1], giving a unique extension in A_3 which is some E_{z_3}.

nodes.name: Part (i): twisted ideal sheaf is stable with polynomial h_{6-d}
nodes.statement: For the first part of~$(i)$, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-points}$(ii)$ it is enough to show that $I_C \otimes \omega_X^{-1}$ is stable with Hilbert polynomial~$h_{6-d}(t)$. Stability is clear by Lemma~\ref{lemma:hd-stable}, and the Hilbert polynomial evidently equals \begin{equation*} h_{{\mathscr{O}}_X}(t+1) - h'_d(t+1) = (3(t+1)(t+2) + 1) - (d(t+1) + 1) = (3t + 6 - d)(t + 1) = h_{6-d}(t). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Part (i): twisted ideal sheaf is stable with polynomial h_{6-d}

nodes.name: Ext(O_L, O_X) = 0 by Serre duality
nodes.statement: For the first part of~$(ii)$ first note that by Serre duality \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{O}}_L,{\mathscr{O}}_X) \cong \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{O}}_X,{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X))^\vee = H^\bullet(L,{\mathscr{O}}_L(-1)) = 0 \end{equation*} since $L \cong {\mathbb{P}}^1$ and $L \cdot K_X = -1$.
nodes.statement_short: Ext(O_L, O_X) = 0 by Serre duality

nodes.name: O_L lies in <A_2, A_3>
nodes.statement: Thus by Theorem~\ref{theorem:dbx} the structure sheaf ${\mathscr{O}}_L$ is contained in the subcategory~$\langle {\mathcal{A}}_2, {\mathcal{A}}_3 \rangle$ of ${\mathbf{D}}(X)$.
nodes.statement_short: O_L lies in <A_2, A_3>

nodes.name: Ext^i(O_L, E_{Z_2}) vanishes unless i = 1, 2
nodes.statement: Next, again by Serre duality \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^i({\mathscr{O}}_L,{\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}) \cong \mathrm{Ext}^{2-i}({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2},{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X))^\vee. \end{equation*} Since ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}$ is a vector bundle and $L$ is a curve, the right hand side is zero unless $i \in \{1, 2\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Ext^i(O_L, E_{Z_2}) vanishes unless i = 1, 2

nodes.name: Ext^2 vanishes by global generation
nodes.statement: On the other hand, ${\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}$ is globally generated by Proposition~\ref{proposition:e-z-big} and~\eqref{eq:cezd}, while ${\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_L(-1)$ has no global sections, hence for $i = 2$ the right hand side is also zero.
nodes.statement_short: Ext^2 vanishes by global generation

nodes.name: Euler characteristic gives Ext = k[-1]
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:chi-ez-f} we have \begin{equation*} \chi({\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2},{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X)) = 2\chi(X,{\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X)) + \chi(X,{\mathscr{O}}_L(2K_X)) - 3r({\mathscr{O}}_L(K_X)) = 2 \cdot h'_1(-1) + h'_1(-2) = -1, \end{equation*} and we conclude that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{O}}_L, {\mathfrak{E}}_{Z_2}) = {\mathsf{k}}[-1]$.
nodes.statement_short: Euler characteristic gives Ext = k[-1]

nodes.name: Unique extension is E_{z_3}
nodes.statement: This means that there is a unique closed point $z_2 \in Z_2$ and a unique extension \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{E}}_{z_2} \to {\mathscr{F}} \to {\mathscr{O}}_L \to 0 \end{equation*} such that ${\mathscr{F}} \in {\mathcal{A}}_3$. It remains to note that ${\mathscr{F}}$ is a sheaf of rank 1, hence there is a unique $z_3 \in Z_3$ such that ${\mathscr{F}} \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{z_3}$.
nodes.statement_short: Unique extension is E_{z_3}

nodes.name: Converse statements
nodes.statement: The converse statements are evident.
nodes.statement_short: Converse statements

nodes.name: Hilbert schemes $F_d(X)$
nodes.statement: F_d(X) := \mathrm{Hilb}_{X,-K_X}(h'_d)
nodes.label: def:fd

nodes.name: Hilbert schemes of lines, conics and twisted cubics
nodes.statement: We have natural isomorphisms of Hilbert schemes \begin{equation*} F_1(X) \cong Z_2 \times Z_3, \qquad F_2(X) \cong {\mathbb{P}}_{Z_2}(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}), \qquad\text{and}\qquad F_3(X) \cong {\mathbb{P}}_{Z_3}(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $F_1(X)\cong Z_2\times Z_3$, $F_2(X)$ and $F_3(X)$ are projectivizations of $p_{2*}\mathscr{E}_{Z_2}$, $p_{3*}\mathscr{E}_{Z_3}$.
conclusions: We have natural isomorphisms of Hilbert schemes \begin{equation*} F_1(X) \cong Z_2 \times Z_3, \qquad F_2(X) \cong {\mathbb{P}}_{Z_2}(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}), \qquad\text{and}\qquad F_3(X) \cong {\mathbb{P}}_{Z_3}(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}). \end{equation*}
nodes.label: proposition:fd-zd

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.9
nodes.statement: Assume $d \in \{2,3\}$. Let ${\mathscr{C}} \subset X \times S$ be a flat $S$-family of subschemes in $X$ with Hilbert polynomial~$h'_d(t)$. Consider the decomposition of the structure sheaf ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \in {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S)$ with respect to the semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S) = \langle {\mathcal{A}}_{3S}^\vee, {\mathcal{A}}_{2S}^\vee, {\mathcal{A}}_{1S}^\vee \rangle, \end{equation*} obtained from the decomposition of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dbx-dual} by the base change $S \to \mathrm{Spec}({\mathsf{k}})$ via~\cite[Theorem~5.6]{kuznetsov2011base}. The argument of Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} together with the result of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oc-decomposition}$(i)$ shows that there is a morphism $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$, a line bundle ${\mathscr{F}}_d$ on $S$, and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}^\vee) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{X \times S} \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0 \end{equation*} The left arrow corresponds to a global section of the bundle $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d^\vee)$, i.e., to a morphism from $p_S^*{\mathscr{F}}_d$ to $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$. We have \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}(p_S^*{\mathscr{F}}_d,(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_d,p_{S*}((\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}))) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_d,f_d^*p_{d*}({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})), \end{equation*} where the first equality follows from adjunction and the second is the base change for the diagram \begin{equation*} \xymatrix@C=5em{ X \times S \ar[r]^-{\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d} \ar[d]_{p_S} & X \times Z_d \ar[d]^{p_d} \\ S \ar[r]^-{f_d} & Z_d } \end{equation*} The flatness over $S$ of the cokernel ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ of the morphism $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}^\vee) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{X \times S}$ is equivalent to the corresponding morphism ${\mathscr{F}}_d \to f_d^*p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$ being nonzero for every closed point $s \in S$. Thus the Hilbert scheme functor $F_d(X)$ is isomorphic to the functor that associates to a scheme $S$ a morphism $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$ and a line subbundle in $f_d^*p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$, hence is represented by the projective bundle ${\mathbb{P}}_{Z_d}(p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$. Now assume $d = 1$ and let ${\mathscr{C}} \subset X \times S$ be a flat family of lines. Decomposing ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ with respect to~\eqref{eq:dbx-s} and using the argument of Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} together with the result of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oc-decomposition}$(ii)$, we conclude that there are morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2$ and ${\mathscr{F}}_3$ on $S$, and an exact sequence \begin{equation} 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{2})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_2) \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{3})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_3) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0. \end{equation} Moreover, the pushforward to $S$ of this sequence gives (again by base change) an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2 \to f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3 \to {\mathscr{O}}_S \to 0. \end{equation*} Since by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez} we know that $f_{d}^*(p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$ is a vector bundle of rank $d$ on $S$, the comparison of determinants gives a relation \begin{equation} {\mathscr{F}}_3^3 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2^{-2} \cong f_{2}^*(\det(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2})) \otimes f_{3}^*(\det(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})^{-1}). \end{equation} Denoting by $f_{23} \colon S \to Z_2 \times Z_3$ the map induced by $f_2$ and $f_3$, we deduce by adjunction and base change \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}(f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2, f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee,f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})) \end{equation*} and note that $f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$ is a line bundle (again by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez}). The flatness over~$S$ of the cokernel ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ of the morphism of~\eqref{eq:o-lines} is equivalent to the pointwise injectivity of the corresponding morphism ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee \to f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$, i.e., to this map being an isomorphism. On the other hand, any line bundle on $S$ can be written as the tensor product of line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee$ satisfying~\eqref{eq:f23-relation} in a unique way. This shows that the Hilbert scheme functor is isomorphic to the functor that associates to a scheme $S$ a pair of morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, hence is represented by $Z_2 \times Z_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose structure sheaves of flat families of curves with respect to the base-changed decompositions as in Theorem 4.5; for d = 2, 3 the data is a map to Z_d and a line subbundle; for lines, a pair of maps with a determinant relation.

nodes.name: Case d = 2, 3
nodes.statement: Assume $d \in \{2,3\}$. Let ${\mathscr{C}} \subset X \times S$ be a flat $S$-family of subschemes in $X$ with Hilbert polynomial~$h'_d(t)$. Consider the decomposition of the structure sheaf ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \in {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S)$ with respect to the semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S) = \langle {\mathcal{A}}_{3S}^\vee, {\mathcal{A}}_{2S}^\vee, {\mathcal{A}}_{1S}^\vee \rangle, \end{equation*} obtained from the decomposition of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dbx-dual} by the base change $S \to \mathrm{Spec}({\mathsf{k}})$ via~\cite[Theorem~5.6]{kuznetsov2011base}. The argument of Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} together with the result of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oc-decomposition}$(i)$ shows that there is a morphism $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$, a line bundle ${\mathscr{F}}_d$ on $S$, and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}^\vee) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{X \times S} \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0 \end{equation*} The left arrow corresponds to a global section of the bundle $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d^\vee)$, i.e., to a morphism from $p_S^*{\mathscr{F}}_d$ to $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$. We have \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}(p_S^*{\mathscr{F}}_d,(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_d,p_{S*}((\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}))) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_d,f_d^*p_{d*}({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})), \end{equation*} where the first equality follows from adjunction and the second is the base change for the diagram \begin{equation*} \xymatrix@C=5em{ X \times S \ar[r]^-{\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d} \ar[d]_{p_S} & X \times Z_d \ar[d]^{p_d} \\ S \ar[r]^-{f_d} & Z_d } \end{equation*} The flatness over $S$ of the cokernel ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ of the morphism $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}^\vee) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{X \times S}$ is equivalent to the corresponding morphism ${\mathscr{F}}_d \to f_d^*p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$ being nonzero for every closed point $s \in S$. Thus the Hilbert scheme functor $F_d(X)$ is isomorphic to the functor that associates to a scheme $S$ a morphism $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$ and a line subbundle in $f_d^*p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$, hence is represented by the projective bundle ${\mathbb{P}}_{Z_d}(p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$.
nodes.statement_short: Case d = 2, 3

nodes.name: Decompose O_C in the dual base-changed decomposition
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathscr{C}} \subset X \times S$ be a flat $S$-family of subschemes in $X$ with Hilbert polynomial~$h'_d(t)$. Consider the decomposition of the structure sheaf ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \in {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S)$ with respect to the semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}(X \times S) = \langle {\mathcal{A}}_{3S}^\vee, {\mathcal{A}}_{2S}^\vee, {\mathcal{A}}_{1S}^\vee \rangle, \end{equation*} obtained from the decomposition of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dbx-dual} by the base change $S \to \mathrm{Spec}({\mathsf{k}})$ via~\cite[Theorem~5.6]{kuznetsov2011base}.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose O_C in the dual base-changed decomposition

nodes.name: Exact sequence from Theorem 4.5 and Lemma 4.8(i)
nodes.statement: The argument of Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} together with the result of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oc-decomposition}$(i)$ shows that there is a morphism $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$, a line bundle ${\mathscr{F}}_d$ on $S$, and an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}^\vee) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{X \times S} \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0 \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Exact sequence from Theorem 4.5 and Lemma 4.8(i)

nodes.name: Translate to a morphism into f_d^* p_d* E
nodes.statement: The left arrow corresponds to a global section of the bundle $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d^\vee)$, i.e., to a morphism from $p_S^*{\mathscr{F}}_d$ to $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$. We have \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}(p_S^*{\mathscr{F}}_d,(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_d,p_{S*}((\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}))) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_d,f_d^*p_{d*}({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})), \end{equation*} where the first equality follows from adjunction and the second is the base change for the diagram \begin{equation*} \xymatrix@C=5em{ X \times S \ar[r]^-{\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d} \ar[d]_{p_S} & X \times Z_d \ar[d]^{p_d} \\ S \ar[r]^-{f_d} & Z_d } \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Translate to a morphism into f_d^* p_d* E

nodes.name: Represented by the projective bundle
nodes.statement: The flatness over $S$ of the cokernel ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ of the morphism $(\mathrm{id}_X \times f_d)^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}^\vee) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_d) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{X \times S}$ is equivalent to the corresponding morphism ${\mathscr{F}}_d \to f_d^*p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$ being nonzero for every closed point $s \in S$. Thus the Hilbert scheme functor $F_d(X)$ is isomorphic to the functor that associates to a scheme $S$ a morphism $f_d \colon S \to Z_d$ and a line subbundle in $f_d^*p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}$, hence is represented by the projective bundle ${\mathbb{P}}_{Z_d}(p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$.
nodes.statement_short: Represented by the projective bundle

nodes.name: Case d = 1
nodes.statement: Now assume $d = 1$ and let ${\mathscr{C}} \subset X \times S$ be a flat family of lines. Decomposing ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ with respect to~\eqref{eq:dbx-s} and using the argument of Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} together with the result of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oc-decomposition}$(ii)$, we conclude that there are morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2$ and ${\mathscr{F}}_3$ on $S$, and an exact sequence \begin{equation} 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{2})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_2) \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{3})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_3) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0. \end{equation} Moreover, the pushforward to $S$ of this sequence gives (again by base change) an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2 \to f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3 \to {\mathscr{O}}_S \to 0. \end{equation*} Since by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez} we know that $f_{d}^*(p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$ is a vector bundle of rank $d$ on $S$, the comparison of determinants gives a relation \begin{equation} {\mathscr{F}}_3^3 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2^{-2} \cong f_{2}^*(\det(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2})) \otimes f_{3}^*(\det(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})^{-1}). \end{equation} Denoting by $f_{23} \colon S \to Z_2 \times Z_3$ the map induced by $f_2$ and $f_3$, we deduce by adjunction and base change \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}(f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2, f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee,f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})) \end{equation*} and note that $f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$ is a line bundle (again by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez}). The flatness over~$S$ of the cokernel ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ of the morphism of~\eqref{eq:o-lines} is equivalent to the pointwise injectivity of the corresponding morphism ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee \to f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$, i.e., to this map being an isomorphism. On the other hand, any line bundle on $S$ can be written as the tensor product of line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee$ satisfying~\eqref{eq:f23-relation} in a unique way. This shows that the Hilbert scheme functor is isomorphic to the functor that associates to a scheme $S$ a pair of morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, hence is represented by $Z_2 \times Z_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Case d = 1

nodes.name: Exact sequence from Theorem 4.5 and Lemma 4.8(ii)
nodes.statement: Decomposing ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ with respect to~\eqref{eq:dbx-s} and using the argument of Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} together with the result of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oc-decomposition}$(ii)$, we conclude that there are morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2$ and ${\mathscr{F}}_3$ on $S$, and an exact sequence \begin{equation} 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{2})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_2) \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{3})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_3) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Exact sequence from Theorem 4.5 and Lemma 4.8(ii)

nodes.name: Exact sequence for a family of lines
nodes.statement: 0 \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{2})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_2) \to (\mathrm{id}_X \times f_{3})^*({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes p_S^*({\mathscr{F}}_3) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}} \to 0.
nodes.label: eq:o-lines

nodes.name: Push forward and compare determinants
nodes.statement: Moreover, the pushforward to $S$ of this sequence gives (again by base change) an exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2 \to f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3 \to {\mathscr{O}}_S \to 0. \end{equation*} Since by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez} we know that $f_{d}^*(p_{d*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d})$ is a vector bundle of rank $d$ on $S$, the comparison of determinants gives a relation \begin{equation} {\mathscr{F}}_3^3 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2^{-2} \cong f_{2}^*(\det(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2})) \otimes f_{3}^*(\det(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})^{-1}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Push forward and compare determinants

nodes.name: Determinant relation for line bundles
nodes.statement: {\mathscr{F}}_3^3 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2^{-2} \cong f_{2}^*(\det(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2})) \otimes f_{3}^*(\det(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})^{-1}).
nodes.label: eq:f23-relation

nodes.name: Hom into a line bundle on Z_2 x Z_3
nodes.statement: Denoting by $f_{23} \colon S \to Z_2 \times Z_3$ the map induced by $f_2$ and $f_3$, we deduce by adjunction and base change \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Hom}(f_{2}^*(p_{2*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_2, f_{3}^*(p_{3*}{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3}) \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3) \cong \mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee,f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})) \end{equation*} and note that $f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$ is a line bundle (again by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ps-ez}).
nodes.statement_short: Hom into a line bundle on Z_2 x Z_3

nodes.name: Flatness means the map is an isomorphism
nodes.statement: The flatness over~$S$ of the cokernel ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{C}}$ of the morphism of~\eqref{eq:o-lines} is equivalent to the pointwise injectivity of the corresponding morphism ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee \to f_{23}^*p_{23*}(p_{X2}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes p_{X3}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_3})$, i.e., to this map being an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Flatness means the map is an isomorphism

nodes.name: Represented by Z_2 x Z_3
nodes.statement: On the other hand, any line bundle on $S$ can be written as the tensor product of line bundles ${\mathscr{F}}_2 \otimes {\mathscr{F}}_3^\vee$ satisfying~\eqref{eq:f23-relation} in a unique way. This shows that the Hilbert scheme functor is isomorphic to the functor that associates to a scheme $S$ a pair of morphisms $f_2 \colon S \to Z_2$ and $f_3 \colon S \to Z_3$, hence is represented by $Z_2 \times Z_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Represented by Z_2 x Z_3

nodes.name: Hilbert scheme $F_4(X)$
nodes.statement: With the same argument one can prove that $p_{2*}({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1})$ is a rank-4 vector bundle on~$Z_2$ and that~$F_4(X) \cong {\mathbb{P}}_{Z_2}(p_{2*}({\mathscr{E}}_{Z_2}^\vee \otimes \omega_X^{-1}))$.
nodes.statement_short: By the same argument $F_4(X)$ is a $\mathbb{P}^3$-bundle over $Z_2$.
nodes.label: remark:f4

nodes.name: Arbitrary base field from Section 5 on
nodes.statement: Starting from this section we assume that ${\mathsf{k}}$ is an arbitrary field of characteristic distinct from~2 and~3, unless something else is specified explicitly.
nodes.section: 5 Families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces

nodes.name: du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement: A family $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ is a {\sf du Val family} of sextic del Pezzo surfaces, if $f$ is a flat projective morphism such that for every geometric point $s \in S$ the fiber ${\mathscr{X}}_s$ of ${\mathscr{X}}$ over $s$ is a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface (Definition~\ref{definition:dp6}), i.e., a normal integral surface with at worst du Val singularities such that $-K_{{\mathscr{X}}_s}$ is an ample Cartier divisor and $K_{{\mathscr{X}}_s}^2 = 6$.
differentia: for every geometric point $s \in S$ the fiber ${\mathscr{X}}_s$ of ${\mathscr{X}}$ over $s$ is a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface
nodes.label: definition:family-dp6

nodes.name: Relative dualizing sheaf of a du Val family is invertible
nodes.statement: Note also that by definition all fibers of $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ are Gorenstein, hence the relative dualizing complex $\omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^\bullet$ when restricted to any fiber of $f$ is an invertible sheaf, hence by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} it is an invertible sheaf on the total space ${\mathscr{X}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fibers are Gorenstein, so by Lemma 4.4 the relative dualizing complex is a line bundle on the total space.

nodes.name: du Val families are stable under base change
nodes.statement: If $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ is a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces then for any base change $S' \to S$ the induced family $f' \colon {\mathscr{X}}' = {\mathscr{X}} \times_S S' \to S'$ is still a du Val family.

nodes.name: Semiorthogonal decomposition for families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement: Assume $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ is a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces. Then there is an~$S$-linear semiorthogonal decomposition \textup{(}compatible with any base change\textup{)} \begin{equation} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}(S), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}) \rangle, \end{equation} where ${\mathscr{Z}}_2 \to S$ and ${\mathscr{Z}}_3 \to S$ are finite flat morphisms of degree $3$ and $2$ respectively, $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ and $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ are Brauer classes of order $2$ and $3$ respectively on them, and the last two components are the twisted derived categories.
nodes.statement_short: For a du Val family $\mathscr{X}\to S$, $\mathbf{D}(\mathscr{X}) = \langle \mathbf{D}(S), \mathbf{D}(\mathscr{Z}_2,\beta_2), \mathbf{D}(\mathscr{Z}_3,\beta_3)\rangle$ with $\mathscr{Z}_2,\mathscr{Z}_3$ finite flat of degrees 3, 2 and Brauer classes of orders 2, 3.
assumptions: Assume $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ is a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces.
conclusions: Then there is an~$S$-linear semiorthogonal decomposition \textup{(}compatible with any base change\textup{)} \begin{equation} \label{eq:sod-dp6} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}(S), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}) \rangle, \end{equation} where ${\mathscr{Z}}_2 \to S$ and ${\mathscr{Z}}_3 \to S$ are finite flat morphisms of degree $3$ and $2$ respectively, $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ and $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ are Brauer classes of order $2$ and $3$ respectively on them, and the last two components are the twisted derived categories.
nodes.label: theorem:sod-dp6

nodes.name: Decomposition (eq:sod-dp6) of $\mathbf{D}(\mathscr{X})$
nodes.statement: {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}(S), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}) \rangle,
nodes.label: eq:sod-dp6

nodes.name: Relative moduli stack $\mathscr{M}_d(\mathscr{X}/S)$
nodes.statement: For $d \in \{2,3,4\}$ let ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ denote the relative moduli stack of semistable sheaves on fibers of ${\mathscr{X}}$ over $S$ with Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ defined in~\eqref{eq:hd}.

nodes.name: Coarse moduli spaces $\mathscr{Z}_d$ and Brauer classes
nodes.statement: For $d \in \{2,3,4\}$ the stack ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is a ${\mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{m}}}$-gerbe over its coarse module space \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) := ({\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S))_{\mathrm{coarse}} \end{equation*} with an obstruction given by a Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ of order \begin{equation} \operatorname{ord} \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \begin{cases} 2, & \text{if $d = 2$ or $d = 4$},\\ 3, & \text{if $d = 3$}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Moreover, there is an isomorphism of the coarse moduli spaces $\sigma_{2,4} \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } {\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ and an automorphism $\sigma_{3,3} \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } {\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)$, such that \begin{equation*} \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1}) = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}) \qquad\text{and}\qquad \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{3,3}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1}). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $\mathscr{M}_d(\mathscr{X}/S)$ is a $\mathrm{G_m}$-gerbe over its coarse space $\mathscr{Z}_d$ with Brauer obstruction of order 2 (d=2,4) or 3 (d=3); $\mathscr{Z}_4\cong\mathscr{Z}_2$ and $\mathscr{Z}_3$ has an involution relating the classes.
conclusions: the stack ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is a ${\mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{m}}}$-gerbe over its coarse module space \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) := ({\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S))_{\mathrm{coarse}} \end{equation*} with an obstruction given by a Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ of order \begin{equation} \label{eq:brauer-order} \operatorname{ord} \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \begin{cases} 2, & \text{if $d = 2$ or $d = 4$},\\ 3, & \text{if $d = 3$}. \end{cases} \end{equation}

Moreover, there is an isomorphism of the coarse moduli spaces $\sigma_{2,4} \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } {\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ and an automorphism $\sigma_{3,3} \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } {\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)$, such that \begin{equation*} \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1}) = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}) \qquad\text{and}\qquad \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{3,3}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1}). \end{equation*}
nodes.label: proposition:md-zd

nodes.name: Orders of the Brauer classes
nodes.statement: \operatorname{ord} \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \begin{cases} 2, & \text{if $d = 2$ or $d = 4$},\\ 3, & \text{if $d = 3$}. \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:brauer-order

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.3
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lemma:hd-stable} all sheaves parameterized by the moduli stack ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ are strictly stable. Therefore, by~\cite[Theorem~4.3.7]{huybrechts1997geometry}, the coarse moduli space ${{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ exists and there is a quasiuniversal family ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ on the fiber product ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d{({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ which has a module structure over a sheaf of Azumaya algebras ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ (defined up to a Morita equivalence) of order equal to the greatest common divisor of the values of the Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ for $t \in {\mathbb{Z}}$. This means that ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is a ${\mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{m}}}$-gerbe over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$. Its obstruction class is given by the Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ of the Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$, and a simple computation of the greatest common divisor of the values of the Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ gives~\eqref{eq:brauer-order}. By Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1}$ on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ provides a family of stable sheaves with Hilbert polynomial $h_4(t)$ and the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1}$ on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ provides a family of stable sheaves with Hilbert polynomial $h_2(t)$. Therefore, the moduli stacks ${\mathscr{M}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ and ${\mathscr{M}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ are isomorphic. Denoting by $\sigma_{2,4}$ the induced isomorphism of the coarse moduli spaces, we conclude that the family $\sigma_{2,4}^*({\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1})$ is a quasiuniversal family on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$. It follows that the pullback of the opposite Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/s)}$ to ${\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is Morita-equivalent to the Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$, hence $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1})$. Since by~\eqref{eq:brauer-order} the order of $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ is~2, this can be also written as~$\sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1})$. The second isomorphism $\sigma_{3,3}$ is constructed in the same way, and with its construction we also get an isomorphism of quasiuniversal families and an equality of Brauer classes.
nodes.statement_short: All sheaves are stable, so Huybrechts-Lehn gives a coarse space with a quasiuniversal family over an Azumaya algebra of order gcd of values of h_d; Theorem 4.5 identifies M_2 with M_4 and M_3 with itself via twisted duals.

nodes.name: All sheaves strictly stable
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lemma:hd-stable} all sheaves parameterized by the moduli stack ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ are strictly stable.
nodes.statement_short: All sheaves strictly stable

nodes.name: Coarse space with quasiuniversal family (cited)
nodes.statement: Therefore, by~\cite[Theorem~4.3.7]{huybrechts1997geometry}, the coarse moduli space ${{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ exists and there is a quasiuniversal family ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ on the fiber product ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d{({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ which has a module structure over a sheaf of Azumaya algebras ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ (defined up to a Morita equivalence) of order equal to the greatest common divisor of the values of the Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ for $t \in {\mathbb{Z}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Coarse space with quasiuniversal family (cited)

nodes.name: Gerbe and order of the Brauer class
nodes.statement: This means that ${\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is a ${\mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{m}}}$-gerbe over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$. Its obstruction class is given by the Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ of the Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$, and a simple computation of the greatest common divisor of the values of the Hilbert polynomial $h_d(t)$ gives~\eqref{eq:brauer-order}.
nodes.statement_short: Gerbe and order of the Brauer class

nodes.name: Twisted duals identify M_2 and M_4
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli} the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1}$ on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ provides a family of stable sheaves with Hilbert polynomial $h_4(t)$ and the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1}$ on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ provides a family of stable sheaves with Hilbert polynomial $h_2(t)$. Therefore, the moduli stacks ${\mathscr{M}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ and ${\mathscr{M}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ are isomorphic.
nodes.statement_short: Twisted duals identify M_2 and M_4

nodes.name: Brauer classes related by sigma_{2,4}
nodes.statement: Denoting by $\sigma_{2,4}$ the induced isomorphism of the coarse moduli spaces, we conclude that the family $\sigma_{2,4}^*({\mathscr{E}}^\vee_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1})$ is a quasiuniversal family on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$. It follows that the pullback of the opposite Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/s)}$ to ${\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is Morita-equivalent to the Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$, hence $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1})$. Since by~\eqref{eq:brauer-order} the order of $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}$ is~2, this can be also written as~$\sigma_{2,4}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{-1})$.
nodes.statement_short: Brauer classes related by sigma_{2,4}

nodes.name: sigma_{3,3} likewise
nodes.statement: The second isomorphism $\sigma_{3,3}$ is constructed in the same way, and with its construction we also get an isomorphism of quasiuniversal families and an equality of Brauer classes.
nodes.statement_short: sigma_{3,3} likewise

nodes.name: Projection $f_d \colon \mathscr{Z}_d \to S$
nodes.statement: We denote by \begin{equation*} f_d \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_d \to S \end{equation*} the natural projection.

nodes.name: Twisted universal family $\mathscr{E}_{\mathscr{Z}_d}$
nodes.statement: We replace the Azumaya algebra ${\mathscr{B}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ by its Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d} \in \mathrm{Br}({\mathscr{Z}}_d)$ and consider the quasiuniversal family as a~$\beta^{-1}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$-twisted family of sheaves on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d$: \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d} \in \mathrm{coh}({\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d, \beta^{-1}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Relation between twisted universal families
nodes.statement: Note that the relation between the quasiuniversal families discussed in Proposition~\ref{proposition:md-zd} in terms of twisted universal families means that there are line bundles ${\mathscr{L}}_{2,4}$ and ${\mathscr{L}}_{3,3}$ on ${\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ and ${\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ respectively, such that \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_4({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{2,4}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{\vee} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1}) \otimes {\mathscr{L}}_{2,4} \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)} = \sigma_{3,3}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3({\mathscr{X}}/S)}^{\vee} \otimes \omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}^{-1}) \otimes {\mathscr{L}}_{3,3}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The twisted universal families of Z_4 and Z_3 are twisted duals of those of Z_2 and Z_3, up to line bundles.

nodes.name: Base change for $\mathscr{M}_d$ and $\mathscr{Z}_d$
nodes.statement: Let $\phi \colon S' \to S$ be a base change and denote ${\mathscr{X}}' := {\mathscr{X}} \times_S S'$. We have \begin{equation} {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S') \cong {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) \times_S S' \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S') \cong {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) \times_S S'. \end{equation} Moreover, isomorphisms~\eqref{eq:md-zd-base-change} are compatible with the universal families, i.e., \begin{equation} \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d} = \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}) \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d} \cong \phi_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}. \end{equation} where we set ${\mathscr{Z}}'_d := {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S')$ and denote the morphisms induced by the base change by $\phi_{\mathscr{X}} \colon {\mathscr{X}}' \to {\mathscr{X}}$, $\phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d} \colon {\mathscr{Z}}'_d \to {\mathscr{Z}}_d$, and $\phi_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d} \colon {\mathscr{X}}' \times_{S'} {\mathscr{Z}}'_d \to {\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Formation of the moduli stacks, coarse spaces, Brauer classes and universal families commutes with base change.
assumptions: Let $\phi \colon S' \to S$ be a base change and denote ${\mathscr{X}}' := {\mathscr{X}} \times_S S'$.
conclusions: We have \begin{equation} \label{eq:md-zd-base-change} {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S') \cong {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) \times_S S' \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S') \cong {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) \times_S S'. \end{equation}

Moreover, isomorphisms~\eqref{eq:md-zd-base-change} are compatible with the universal families, i.e., \begin{equation}\label{eq:ced-base-change} \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d} = \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}) \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d} \cong \phi_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}. \end{equation}
nodes.label: lemma:md-zd-base-change

nodes.name: Base change of moduli stacks and coarse spaces
nodes.statement: {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S') \cong {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) \times_S S' \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}'/S') \cong {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S) \times_S S'.
nodes.label: eq:md-zd-base-change

nodes.name: Base change of Brauer classes and universal families
nodes.statement: \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d} = \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}) \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d} \cong \phi_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*{\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}.
nodes.label: eq:ced-base-change

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.4
nodes.statement: The first isomorphism in~\eqref{eq:md-zd-base-change} is clear from the definition of a relative moduli space, and the second follows from the GIT construction of the coarse moduli space. Since the pullback of a universal family is a $\phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*(\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d})$-twisted family of stable sheaves on fibers of ${\mathscr{X}}'$ over $S'$, the equality of the Brauer classes and the isomorphism of universal families follow.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the definition of the relative moduli functor and the GIT construction of the coarse space.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.5
nodes.statement: Considering base changes to geometric points of $S$ and using Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli}, we obtain
nodes.statement_short: Base change to geometric points (Lemma 5.4) combined with Theorem 4.5.

nodes.name: Fibers of the relative moduli spaces
nodes.statement: For any geometric point $s \in S$ there are isomorphisms \begin{equation} {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \cong {\mathscr{M}}_d(X), \qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \cong Z_d \qquad\text{and}\qquad i_{Z_d}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}, \end{equation} where $X = {\mathscr{X}}_s$ is the fiber of ${\mathscr{X}}$ over $s$ and $i_{Z_d} \colon Z_d \cong {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \hookrightarrow {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is the natural embedding.
nodes.statement_short: Over a geometric point, $\mathscr{M}_d$, $\mathscr{Z}_d$ and the universal family restrict to $\mathscr{M}_d(X)$, $Z_d$ and $\mathscr{E}_{Z_d}$.
assumptions: For any geometric point $s \in S$
conclusions: there are isomorphisms \begin{equation} \label{eq:m-z-e-s} {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \cong {\mathscr{M}}_d(X), \qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \cong Z_d \qquad\text{and}\qquad i_{Z_d}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}, \end{equation} where $X = {\mathscr{X}}_s$ is the fiber of ${\mathscr{X}}$ over $s$ and $i_{Z_d} \colon Z_d \cong {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \hookrightarrow {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)$ is the natural embedding.
nodes.label: corollary:S-s

nodes.name: Fiberwise identifications
nodes.statement: {\mathscr{M}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \cong {\mathscr{M}}_d(X), \qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_d({\mathscr{X}}/S)_s \cong Z_d \qquad\text{and}\qquad i_{Z_d}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d},
nodes.label: eq:m-z-e-s

nodes.name: Finiteness and flatness of $\mathscr{Z}_2, \mathscr{Z}_3$ over S
nodes.statement: The maps $f_2 \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_2 \to S$ and $f_3 \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_3 \to S$ are finite flat maps of degree $3$ and $2$ respectively. The relative dualizing complexes $\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2/S}^\bullet$ and $\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3/S}^\bullet$ are line bundles.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathscr{Z}_2\to S$ and $\mathscr{Z}_3\to S$ are finite flat of degrees 3 and 2 with invertible relative dualizing complexes.
conclusions: The maps $f_2 \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_2 \to S$ and $f_3 \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_3 \to S$ are finite flat maps of degree $3$ and $2$ respectively.
The relative dualizing complexes $\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2/S}^\bullet$ and $\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3/S}^\bullet$ are line bundles.
nodes.label: lemma:zd-flat

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.6
nodes.statement: Since flatness can be verified on an \'etale covering (note that formation of schemes ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ is compatible with base changes by~\eqref{eq:md-zd-base-change}) and the moduli stack of du Val sextic del Pezzo surfaces is smooth by Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli-stack-dp6}, we may assume that $S$ is smooth over ${\mathsf{k}}$, hence reduced. Since ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ is proper over $S$, it is enough to show that the (scheme-theoretic) fiber of ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ over any geometric point ${{s}} \in S$ is zero-dimensional of length~$6/d$. But as it was mentioned in Corollary~\ref{corollary:S-s}, the fiber $({\mathscr{Z}}_d)_s$ is identified with the zero-dimensional scheme~$Z_d$ associated with the surface $X = {\mathscr{X}}_s$, and hence its length is indeed~$6/d$, see Corollary~\ref{corollary:dbx-z2-z3}. Since $f_d$ is flat, to check that the relative dualizing complex is a line bundle, it is enough to check that each fiber of $f_d$ is a Gorenstein scheme, which holds true by~\eqref{eq:m-z-e-s} and Corollary~\ref{corollary:dbx-z2-z3}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to smooth S using smoothness of the moduli stack and base change; fibers are the length-6/d Gorenstein schemes Z_d, so f_d is finite flat with invertible dualizing complex.

nodes.name: Reduce to smooth (reduced) base
nodes.statement: Since flatness can be verified on an \'etale covering (note that formation of schemes ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ is compatible with base changes by~\eqref{eq:md-zd-base-change}) and the moduli stack of du Val sextic del Pezzo surfaces is smooth by Theorem~\ref{theorem:moduli-stack-dp6}, we may assume that $S$ is smooth over ${\mathsf{k}}$, hence reduced.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to smooth (reduced) base

nodes.name: Reduce to fiber length
nodes.statement: Since ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ is proper over $S$, it is enough to show that the (scheme-theoretic) fiber of ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ over any geometric point ${{s}} \in S$ is zero-dimensional of length~$6/d$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to fiber length

nodes.name: Fibers are Z_d of length 6/d
nodes.statement: But as it was mentioned in Corollary~\ref{corollary:S-s}, the fiber $({\mathscr{Z}}_d)_s$ is identified with the zero-dimensional scheme~$Z_d$ associated with the surface $X = {\mathscr{X}}_s$, and hence its length is indeed~$6/d$, see Corollary~\ref{corollary:dbx-z2-z3}.
nodes.statement_short: Fibers are Z_d of length 6/d

nodes.name: Gorenstein fibers give invertible dualizing complex
nodes.statement: Since $f_d$ is flat, to check that the relative dualizing complex is a line bundle, it is enough to check that each fiber of $f_d$ is a Gorenstein scheme, which holds true by~\eqref{eq:m-z-e-s} and Corollary~\ref{corollary:dbx-z2-z3}.
nodes.statement_short: Gorenstein fibers give invertible dualizing complex

nodes.name: Conventions for $\mathscr{Z}_1$
nodes.statement: For convenience we also define ${\mathscr{Z}}_1 = S$, set $f_1 \colon {\mathscr{Z}}_1 \to S$ to be the identity map, set $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_1}$ to be the trivial Brauer class, and ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_1} = {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}$.

nodes.name: Projections $p$ and $p_d$
nodes.statement: Let $p \colon {\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d \to {\mathscr{X}}$ and $p_d \colon {\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d \to {\mathscr{Z}}_d$ be the projections.

nodes.name: Fiber square for the universal family
nodes.statement: \vcenter{\xymatrix@C=5em{ {\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d \ar[r]^{p_d} \ar[d]_{p} & {\mathscr{Z}}_d \ar[d]^{f_d} \\ {\mathscr{X}} \ar[r]_-f & S }}
nodes.label: diagram:x-s-z

nodes.name: Flatness and finite Ext-amplitude of $\mathscr{E}_{\mathscr{Z}_d}$
nodes.statement: For each $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ is flat over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ and has finite $\mathrm{Ext}$-amplitude over ${\mathscr{X}}$.
nodes.statement_short: The universal kernels are flat over Z_d and have finite Ext-amplitude over the total space.
assumptions: For each $d \in \{1,2,3\}$
conclusions: the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ is flat over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ and has finite $\mathrm{Ext}$-amplitude over ${\mathscr{X}}$.
nodes.label: lemma:ezd-tor-ext

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.7
nodes.statement: For $d \in \{2,3\}$ the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ is flat over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ since it comes from a quasiuniversal family for a moduli problem. Since $p$ is a finite map (Lemma~\ref{lemma:zd-flat}), to check that ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ has finite $\mathrm{Ext}$-amplitude over ${\mathscr{X}}$, it is enough (\cite[Lemma~10.40]{kuznetsov2006hyperplane}) to show that $p_*{\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ has finite $\mathrm{Ext}$-amplitude on ${\mathscr{X}}$. But this is in fact a locally free sheaf by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} and Proposition~\ref{proposition:e-z-big}. In case $d = 1$ both properties are evident.
nodes.statement_short: Flatness from the moduli interpretation; finite Ext-amplitude because p is finite and p_* of the kernel is locally free.

nodes.name: Flatness from quasiuniversality
nodes.statement: For $d \in \{2,3\}$ the sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ is flat over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ since it comes from a quasiuniversal family for a moduli problem.
nodes.statement_short: Flatness from quasiuniversality

nodes.name: Finite Ext-amplitude via locally free pushforward
nodes.statement: Since $p$ is a finite map (Lemma~\ref{lemma:zd-flat}), to check that ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ has finite $\mathrm{Ext}$-amplitude over ${\mathscr{X}}$, it is enough (\cite[Lemma~10.40]{kuznetsov2006hyperplane}) to show that $p_*{\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}$ has finite $\mathrm{Ext}$-amplitude on ${\mathscr{X}}$. But this is in fact a locally free sheaf by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} and Proposition~\ref{proposition:e-z-big}.
nodes.statement_short: Finite Ext-amplitude via locally free pushforward

nodes.name: Case d = 1
nodes.statement: In case $d = 1$ both properties are evident.
nodes.statement_short: Case d = 1

nodes.name: Fourier-Mukai functors $\Phi_d$
nodes.statement: \Phi_d = \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}} := p_*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d} \otimes p_d^*(-)) \colon {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}) \to {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}).
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_d = p_*(\mathscr{E}_{\mathscr{Z}_d}\otimes p_d^*(-))$ from the twisted derived category of $\mathscr{Z}_d$ to $\mathbf{D}(\mathscr{X})$.
nodes.label: eq:phid-definition

nodes.name: Properties and right adjoint of $\Phi_d$
nodes.statement: The functor $\Phi_d$ is $S$-linear, preserves boundedness and perfectness, and its right adjoint functor is \begin{equation} \Phi_d^! \colon {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) \to {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}),\qquad \Phi_d^!({\mathscr{G}}) \cong p_{d*}\mathrm{R}\mathscr{H}\mathit{om}({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d},p^!{\mathscr{G}}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_d$ is S-linear, preserves boundedness and perfectness, with right adjoint $p_{d*}\mathrm{RHom}(\mathscr{E}, p^!-)$.
conclusions: The functor $\Phi_d$ is $S$-linear, preserves boundedness and perfectness,

and its right adjoint functor is \begin{equation} \label{eq:phid-shriek} \Phi_d^! \colon {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) \to {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}),\qquad \Phi_d^!({\mathscr{G}}) \cong p_{d*}\mathrm{R}\mathscr{H}\mathit{om}({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d},p^!{\mathscr{G}}). \end{equation}
nodes.label: lemma:phi-d-shriek

nodes.name: Right adjoint $\Phi_d^!$
nodes.statement: \Phi_d^! \colon {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) \to {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}),\qquad \Phi_d^!({\mathscr{G}}) \cong p_{d*}\mathrm{R}\mathscr{H}\mathit{om}({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d},p^!{\mathscr{G}}).
nodes.label: eq:phid-shriek

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.8
nodes.statement: This holds by Lemma~\ref{lemma:ezd-tor-ext} and \cite[Lemma~2.4]{kuznetsov2006hyperplane}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.7 plus Kuznetsov's general lemma on Fourier-Mukai functors.

nodes.name: Precise form of the main decomposition
nodes.statement: {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle \Phi_1({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_1,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_1})), \Phi_2({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2})), \Phi_3({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3})) \rangle
nodes.statement_short: The goal: $\mathbf{D}(\mathscr{X}) = \langle \Phi_1(\ldots), \Phi_2(\ldots), \Phi_3(\ldots)\rangle$ is an S-linear semiorthogonal decomposition.
nodes.label: eq:dbcx-again

nodes.name: Fourier-Mukai form of $\Phi_d^!$
nodes.statement: We have an isomorphism of functors \begin{equation*} \Phi_d^!({\mathscr{G}}) \cong p_{d*}({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S} \otimes p^*({\mathscr{G}})), \end{equation*} where ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee := \mathrm{R}\mathscr{H}\mathit{om}({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d},{\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d})$ is a coherent sheaf flat over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$. The kernel~${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$ of this functor is compativle with base changes, i.e., if $\phi \colon S' \to S$ is a base change, then \begin{equation*} \phi_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^{\prime*}\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d/S'}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_d^!$ is the Fourier-Mukai functor with kernel $\mathscr{E}^\vee\otimes p_d^*\omega_{\mathscr{Z}_d/S}$, a flat sheaf compatible with base change.
conclusions: We have an isomorphism of functors \begin{equation*} \Phi_d^!({\mathscr{G}}) \cong p_{d*}({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S} \otimes p^*({\mathscr{G}})), \end{equation*} where ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee := \mathrm{R}\mathscr{H}\mathit{om}({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d},{\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d})$ is a coherent sheaf flat over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$.

The kernel~${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$ of this functor is compativle with base changes, i.e., if $\phi \colon S' \to S$ is a base change, then \begin{equation*} \phi_{{\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^{\prime*}\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d/S'}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lemma:phid-shriek-other

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.9
nodes.statement: For the first part it is enough to show that \begin{equation} \mathrm{R}\mathscr{H}\mathit{om}({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d},p^!{\mathscr{G}}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S} \otimes p^*({\mathscr{G}}). \end{equation} For this we use an argument of Neeman from~\cite[Theorem~5.4]{neeman1996grothendieck}. First, the functor in the right hand side of~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} commutes with arbitrary direct sums since the pullback and the tensor product functors do. The functor in the left hand side is right adjoint to the functor~$p_*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d} \otimes (-))$. The latter functor preserves perfectness by an argument analogous to that of Lemma~\ref{lemma:phi-d-shriek}, hence the former commutes with direct sums by~\cite[Theorem~5.1]{neeman1996grothendieck}. Further, if ${\mathscr{G}}$ is a perfect complex, then $p^!({\mathscr{G}}) \cong p^*({\mathscr{G}}) \otimes p_d^*\omega^\bullet_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:zd-flat} the dualizing complex~$\omega^\bullet_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$ is a line bundle $\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$, hence $p^!({\mathscr{G}})$ is a perfect complex, and~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} in this case follows. Now the Neeman's trick comes. There is a natural transformation from the functor in the right hand side of~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} to the functor in the left hand side. The subcategory of objects on which this transformation is an isomorphism is a triangulated subcategory of the unbounded derived category of ${\mathscr{X}}$ which contains all perfect complexes and is closed under arbitrary direct sums, hence is the whole category. This proves~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} for all ${\mathscr{G}}$. The fact that ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee$ is a sheaf flat over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ follows from the isomorphisms in the proof of Proposition~\ref{proposition:md-zd} since $\omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}$ is a line bundle. Using Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change} we deduce the required base change isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Neeman's trick: both sides commute with direct sums and agree on perfect complexes (dualizing complex is a line bundle), hence agree everywhere; flatness and base change from Proposition 5.3 and Lemma 5.4.

nodes.name: Reduce to (eq:isomorphism-functors); use Neeman's argument
nodes.statement: For the first part it is enough to show that \begin{equation} \mathrm{R}\mathscr{H}\mathit{om}({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d},p^!{\mathscr{G}}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S} \otimes p^*({\mathscr{G}}). \end{equation} For this we use an argument of Neeman from~\cite[Theorem~5.4]{neeman1996grothendieck}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to (eq:isomorphism-functors); use Neeman's argument

nodes.name: Isomorphism of functors to be proved
nodes.statement: \mathrm{R}\mathscr{H}\mathit{om}({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d},p^!{\mathscr{G}}) \cong {\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee \otimes p_d^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S} \otimes p^*({\mathscr{G}}).
nodes.label: eq:isomorphism-functors

nodes.name: Both sides commute with direct sums
nodes.statement: First, the functor in the right hand side of~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} commutes with arbitrary direct sums since the pullback and the tensor product functors do. The functor in the left hand side is right adjoint to the functor~$p_*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d} \otimes (-))$. The latter functor preserves perfectness by an argument analogous to that of Lemma~\ref{lemma:phi-d-shriek}, hence the former commutes with direct sums by~\cite[Theorem~5.1]{neeman1996grothendieck}.
nodes.statement_short: Both sides commute with direct sums

nodes.name: Isomorphism on perfect complexes
nodes.statement: Further, if ${\mathscr{G}}$ is a perfect complex, then $p^!({\mathscr{G}}) \cong p^*({\mathscr{G}}) \otimes p_d^*\omega^\bullet_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$. By Lemma~\ref{lemma:zd-flat} the dualizing complex~$\omega^\bullet_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$ is a line bundle $\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d/S}$, hence $p^!({\mathscr{G}})$ is a perfect complex, and~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} in this case follows.
nodes.statement_short: Isomorphism on perfect complexes

nodes.name: Extend to all objects by Neeman's trick
nodes.statement: Now the Neeman's trick comes. There is a natural transformation from the functor in the right hand side of~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} to the functor in the left hand side. The subcategory of objects on which this transformation is an isomorphism is a triangulated subcategory of the unbounded derived category of ${\mathscr{X}}$ which contains all perfect complexes and is closed under arbitrary direct sums, hence is the whole category. This proves~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-functors} for all ${\mathscr{G}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Extend to all objects by Neeman's trick

nodes.name: Flatness and base change of the kernel
nodes.statement: The fact that ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^\vee$ is a sheaf flat over ${\mathscr{Z}}_d$ follows from the isomorphisms in the proof of Proposition~\ref{proposition:md-zd} since $\omega_{{\mathscr{X}}/S}$ is a line bundle. Using Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change} we deduce the required base change isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Flatness and base change of the kernel

nodes.name: Base-changed functor $\Phi'_d$
nodes.statement: Given a base change~$\phi \colon S' \to S$, we abbreviate the Fourier--Mukai functor $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}'_d}} \colon {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}'_d) \to {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}')$ as~$\Phi'_d$.

nodes.name: Base change compatibility of $\Phi_d$ and $\Phi_d^!$
nodes.statement: The functors $\Phi_d$ and $\Phi_d^!$ are $S$-linear and compatible with base changes, i.e., \begin{align*} \Phi'_d \circ \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^* &\cong \phi_{{\mathscr{X}}}^* \circ \Phi_d, & \phi_{{\mathscr{X}}*} \circ \Phi'_d &\cong \Phi_d \circ \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d*}, \\ \Phi^{\prime!}_d \circ \phi_{{\mathscr{X}}}^* &\cong \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^* \circ \Phi_d^!, & \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d*} \circ \Phi^{\prime!}_d &\cong \Phi_d^! \circ \phi_{{\mathscr{X}}*}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The functors and their right adjoints commute with pullbacks and pushforwards along base changes.
conclusions: The functors $\Phi_d$ and $\Phi_d^!$ are $S$-linear and compatible with base changes, i.e., \begin{align*} \Phi'_d \circ \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^* &\cong \phi_{{\mathscr{X}}}^* \circ \Phi_d, & \phi_{{\mathscr{X}}*} \circ \Phi'_d &\cong \Phi_d \circ \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d*}, \\ \Phi^{\prime!}_d \circ \phi_{{\mathscr{X}}}^* &\cong \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}^* \circ \Phi_d^!, & \phi_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d*} \circ \Phi^{\prime!}_d &\cong \Phi_d^! \circ \phi_{{\mathscr{X}}*}. \end{align*}
nodes.label: lemma:phid-linear

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.10
nodes.statement: For a Fourier--Mukai functor compatibilities with base changes are proved in~\cite[Lemma~2.42]{kuznetsov2006hyperplane} (the assumption of finiteness of $\mathrm{Tor}$-dimension of the base change morphism is only used in the second half of that lemma). It remains to note that both $\Phi_d$ and $\Phi_d^!$ are Fourier--Mukai functors (the first by definition~\eqref{eq:phid-definition} and the second by Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-shriek-other}).
nodes.statement_short: Base change for Fourier-Mukai functors (Kuznetsov), applied to both functors via Lemma 5.9.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2
nodes.statement: Take $d_1,d_2 \in \{1,2,3\}$ and consider the diagram \begin{equation*} \xymatrix{ & {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1} \times_S {\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2} \ar[dl]_{\mathrm{pr}_{1,2}} \ar[d]^{\mathrm{pr}_{1,3}} \ar[dr]^{\mathrm{pr}_{2,3}} \\ {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1} \times_S {\mathscr{X}} & {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2} & {\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2} } \end{equation*} A standard computation shows that the composition of functors $\Phi_{d_2}^! \circ \Phi_{d_1}$ is a Fourier--Mukai functor given by the object \begin{equation} \mathrm{pr}_{1,3*}(\mathrm{pr}_{2,3}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2}}^\vee \otimes p_{d_2}^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2}/S}) \otimes \mathrm{pr}_{1,2}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1}})) \in {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2}, \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d_1}}^{-1} \boxtimes \beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d_2}}). \end{equation} Let us prove that $\Phi_d$ is fully faithful for each $d \in \{1,2,3\}$. For this it is enough to check that the object~\eqref{eq:convolution} in case $d_1 = d_2 = d$ is isomorphic (via the unit of adjunction morphism) to the structure sheaf of the diagonal. Since the unit of the adjunction is induced by a morphism of kernels \cite{anno2012adjunction}, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} it is enough to check that for any geometric point $s \in S$ we have \begin{equation} i_{Z_d \times Z_d}^*(\mathrm{pr}_{1,3*}(\mathrm{pr}_{2,3}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}}^\vee \otimes p_{d}^*\omega_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}/S}) \otimes \mathrm{pr}_{1,2}^*({\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_{d}}))) \cong \delta_*{\mathscr{O}}_{Z_d} \in {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d \times Z_d) \end{equation} where $i_{Z_d \times Z_d} \colon Z_d \times Z_d \to {\mathscr{Z}}_d \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_d$ is the natural embedding and $\delta \colon Z_d \to Z_d \times Z_d$ is the diagonal. Using base change and isomorphisms of Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-shriek-other}, we can rewrite the left hand side of~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-diagonal} as the Fourier--Mukai kernel of the functor \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d) \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}\ } {\mathbf{D}}(X) \xrightarrow{\ \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}^!\ } {\mathbf{D}}(Z_d), \end{equation*} where the functor $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}$ is identified in Proposition~\ref{proposition:fm-zd} with the equivalence ${\mathbf{D}}(Z_d) \cong {\mathcal{A}}_d \subset {\mathbf{D}}(X)$, and~$\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}^!$ is its right adjoint. This composition is isomorphic to the identity, since the functor $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_d}}$ is fully faithful, hence we have~\eqref{eq:isomorphism-diagonal}. Therefore, the functor $\Phi_d$ is fully faithful. Next, let us prove that the subcategories $\Phi_d({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d})) \subset {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$ for $1 \le d \le 3$ are semiorthogonal. For this it is enough to check that the object~\eqref{eq:convolution} in case $d_1 < d_2$ is zero. Again, using Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise} and base change isomorphisms of Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-shriek-other} we reduce to the case of $S = \mathrm{Spec}({\mathsf{k}})$ with algebraically closed ${\mathsf{k}}$. In the latter case, the required vanishing follows from semiorthogonality of the subcategories $\Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_{Z_{d_i}}}({\mathbf{D}}(Z_{d_i})) = {\mathcal{A}}_{d_i}$ in ${\mathbf{D}}(X)$. Finally, let us prove that the subcategories $\Phi_d({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d})) \subset {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$ for $1 \le d \le 3$ generate ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$. Take any ${\mathscr{G}} \in {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$ and set \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{G}}_2 := \mathrm{Cone}(\Phi_3\Phi_3^!{\mathscr{G}} \to {\mathscr{G}}), \qquad {\mathscr{G}}_1 := \mathrm{Cone}(\Phi_2\Phi_2^!{\mathscr{G}}_2 \to {\mathscr{G}}_2), \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{G}}_0 := \mathrm{Cone}(\Phi_1\Phi_1^!{\mathscr{G}}_1 \to {\mathscr{G}}_1). \end{equation*} From full faithfulness and semiorthogonality it easily follows that $\Phi_1^!({\mathscr{G}}_0) = \Phi_2^!({\mathscr{G}}_0) = \Phi_3^!({\mathscr{G}}_0) = 0$. Then Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-linear} implies that for any geometric point $s \in S$ setting ${\mathscr{G}}_{0s} = i_{X}^*({\mathscr{G}}_0) \in {\mathbf{D}}(X)$ to be the restriction of ${\mathscr{G}}_0$ to the fiber $X = {\mathscr{X}}_s$, we have $\Phi_d^!({\mathscr{G}}_{0s}) = 0$ for all $d$. By semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbx-dz} this means that ${\mathscr{G}}_{0s} = 0$. Hence by Lemma~\ref{lemma:fiberwise}$(i)$ we have ${\mathscr{G}}_0 = 0$. Thus we have a chain of morphisms \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{G}} =: {\mathscr{G}}_3 \to {\mathscr{G}}_2 \to {\mathscr{G}}_1 \to {\mathscr{G}}_0 = 0 \end{equation*} with $\mathrm{Cone}({\mathscr{G}}_{d} \to {\mathscr{G}}_{d-1}) \in \Phi_d({\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{Z}}_d,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_d}))$, which proves the required semiorthogonal decomposition. This semiorthogonal decomposition is $S$-linear since by Lemma~\ref{lemma:phi-d-shriek} its embedding functors~$\Phi_d$ are $S$-linear, and its compatibility with base changes follows from~\cite[Theorem~6.4]{kuznetsov2011base} together with Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-linear} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:md-zd-base-change}.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the convolution kernels of $\Phi^!_{d_2}\Phi_{d_1}$ and check fiberwise (Lemma 4.4) that they are the diagonal or zero, reducing to the single-surface decomposition; generation follows since the residual object vanishes on every fiber.

Then Lemma~\ref{lemma:phid-linear} implies that for any geometric point $s \in S$ setting ${\mathscr{G}}_{0s} = i_{X}^*({\mathscr{G}}_0) \in {\mathbf{D}}(X)$ to be the restriction of ${\mathscr{G}}_0$ to the fiber $X = {\mathscr{X}}_s$, we have $\Phi_d^!({\mathscr{G}}_{0s}) = 0$ for all $d$. nodes.name: Admissibility and perfect version of the family decomposition
nodes.statement: The components of the semiorthogonal decomposition~\eqref{eq:sod-dp6} are admissible and their projection functors have finite cohomological amplitude. Moreover, the functors $\Phi_d$ preserve perfectness and induce a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} {\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle \Phi_1({\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}(S)), \Phi_2({\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}({\mathscr{Z}}_2,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2})), \Phi_3({\mathbf{D}}^{\mathrm{perf}}({\mathscr{Z}}_3,\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3})) \rangle. \end{equation}
