nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.4
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{proposition:fd-md} there is a pair of rank 3 vector bundles ${\mathscr{W}}_1$ and ${\mathscr{W}}_2$ on $S$ such that \begin{equation*} F_3({\mathscr{X}}/S) = {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_1) \sqcup {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_2). \end{equation*} Moreover, the restrictions of the universal sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_3 = {\mathscr{X}} \sqcup {\mathscr{X}}$ to the two components are line bundles defining regular maps ${\mathscr{X}} \to {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_1)$ and ${\mathscr{X}} \to {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_2)$ respectively. Thus, the induced map \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{X}} \to {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_1) \times_S {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_2) \end{equation*} is a closed embedding. Zariski locally the bundles ${\mathscr{W}}_1$ and ${\mathscr{W}}_2$ are trivial, hence we obtain the required local presentation of ${\mathscr{X}}$. The Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ vanishes Zariski locally by Proposition~\ref{proposition:dp-p2p2} and~${\mathscr{Z}}_2$ is regular by Proposition~\ref{proposition:smoothness}, hence $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2} = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: F_3 is a disjoint union of two P^2-bundles; the universal line bundles embed the family into their product; then Proposition 6.2 and the regularity criterion kill beta_2.

nodes.name: F_3 is a union of two P^2-bundles
nodes.statement: By Proposition~\ref{proposition:fd-md} there is a pair of rank 3 vector bundles ${\mathscr{W}}_1$ and ${\mathscr{W}}_2$ on $S$ such that \begin{equation*} F_3({\mathscr{X}}/S) = {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_1) \sqcup {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_2). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: F_3 is a union of two P^2-bundles

nodes.name: Closed embedding into the product of P^2-bundles; local presentation
nodes.statement: Moreover, the restrictions of the universal sheaf ${\mathscr{E}}_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ on ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S {\mathscr{Z}}_3 = {\mathscr{X}} \sqcup {\mathscr{X}}$ to the two components are line bundles defining regular maps ${\mathscr{X}} \to {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_1)$ and ${\mathscr{X}} \to {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_2)$ respectively. Thus, the induced map \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{X}} \to {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_1) \times_S {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{W}}_2) \end{equation*} is a closed embedding. Zariski locally the bundles ${\mathscr{W}}_1$ and ${\mathscr{W}}_2$ are trivial, hence we obtain the required local presentation of ${\mathscr{X}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Closed embedding into the product of P^2-bundles; local presentation

nodes.name: beta_2 vanishes
nodes.statement: The Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ vanishes Zariski locally by Proposition~\ref{proposition:dp-p2p2} and~${\mathscr{Z}}_2$ is regular by Proposition~\ref{proposition:smoothness}, hence $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2} = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: beta_2 vanishes

nodes.name: Segre embedding of $\mathbb{P}(V_1)\times\mathbb{P}(V_2)\times\mathbb{P}(V_3)$
nodes.statement: We denote by $V_1$, $V_2$, and $V_3$ three vector spaces of dimension 2 and let \begin{equation*} {\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3) \hookrightarrow {\mathbb{P}}(V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes V_3) \end{equation*} be the Segre embedding.

nodes.name: Hyperplane section $X_b$
nodes.statement: For a trilinear form $b \in V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee$ we denote by \begin{equation} X_b := ({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)) \cap {\mathbb{P}}(b^\perp) \subset {\mathbb{P}}(V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes V_3) \end{equation} the corresponding hyperplane section, where $b^\perp \subset V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes V_3$ is the annihilator hyperplane of $b$.

nodes.name: Definition of $X_b$
nodes.statement: X_b := ({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)) \cap {\mathbb{P}}(b^\perp) \subset {\mathbb{P}}(V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes V_3)
nodes.label: eq:xb

nodes.name: Orbits of trilinear forms on $(\mathbb{C}^2)^{\otimes 3}$
nodes.statement: Recall that the group ${\mathrm{G}} := (\mathrm{PGL}(V_1) \times \mathrm{PGL}(V_2) \times \mathrm{PGL}(V_3)) \rtimes {\mathfrak{S}}_3$ acts on ${\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)$ with four orbits. The orbits closures are: \begin{itemize} \item ${\mathrm{O}}_3 = {\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2^\vee) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3^\vee)$; \item $\overline{\mathrm{O}}_4 = ({\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)) \cup ({\mathbb{P}}(V_2^\vee) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)) \cup ({\mathbb{P}}(V_3^\vee) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee))$; \item $\overline{\mathrm{O}}_6 = ({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3))^\vee$ is the projectively dual quartic hypersurface; and \item $\overline{\mathrm{O}}_7 = {\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)$ \end{itemize} (we use the dimensions of the orbits as indices).
nodes.statement_short: The group (PGL_2)^3 x S_3 acts on P(V_1* x V_2* x V_3*) with four orbits of dimensions 3, 4, 6, 7.

nodes.name: Cayley hyperdeterminant
nodes.statement: The equation of the quartic hypersurface $\overline{\mathrm{O}}_6$ is given by the Cayley's hyperdeterminant, see~\cite[14.1.7]{gkz1994}.

nodes.name: When $X_b$ is a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface
nodes.statement: Assume the base field ${\mathsf{k}}$ is algebraically closed. The hyperplane section $X_b$ defined by~\textup{\eqref{eq:xb}} is a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface if and only if $b \in {\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee) \setminus \overline{\mathrm{O}}_4$. Furthermore, $X_b$ is smooth if and only if $b \in {\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee) \setminus \overline{\mathrm{O}}_6$.
nodes.statement_short: $X_b$ is a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface iff b is outside the closure of the 4-dimensional orbit, and smooth iff outside the Cayley quartic.
assumptions: Assume the base field ${\mathsf{k}}$ is algebraically closed.
conclusions: The hyperplane section $X_b$ defined by~\textup{\eqref{eq:xb}} is a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface if and only if $b \in {\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee) \setminus \overline{\mathrm{O}}_4$.
Furthermore, $X_b$ is smooth if and only if $b \in {\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee) \setminus \overline{\mathrm{O}}_6$.
nodes.label: lemma:xb-duval

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.5
nodes.statement: Indeed, choosing a representative of each orbit, it is easy to see that $X_b$ is smooth, if $b \in {\mathrm{O}}_7$; has one $A_1$ singularity (and is of type 1), if $b \in {\mathrm{O}}_6$; is a union of a smooth quadric and a quartic scroll, if~$b \in {\mathrm{O}}_4$; and is a union of three quadrics, if $b \in {\mathrm{O}}_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Check a representative of each orbit.

nodes.name: Base S of the family of hyperplane sections of (P^1)^3
nodes.statement: Consider the open subset \begin{equation*} S := {\mathrm{O}}_6 \cup {\mathrm{O}}_7 = {\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee) \setminus \overline{\mathrm{O}}_4 \subset {\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Universal family of hyperplane sections of P^1 x P^1 x P^1
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathscr{L}} \subset V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_S$ be the tautological line bundle, let ${\mathscr{L}}^\perp \subset V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes V_3 \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_S$ be its rank 7 annihilator, and let \begin{equation} {\mathscr{X}} := ({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)) \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes V_3)} {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{L}}^\perp) \end{equation} be the corresponding du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces.

nodes.name: Family $\mathscr{X}$ of hyperplane sections of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^3$
nodes.statement: {\mathscr{X}} := ({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)) \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes V_3)} {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{L}}^\perp)
nodes.label: eq:cx-p1p1p1

nodes.name: Double cover $\mathscr{D}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}$
nodes.statement: Denote by ${{\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}} \to {\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)$ the double covering branched along the Cayley quartic hypersurface~$\overline{\mathrm{O}}_6$.

nodes.name: Family of hyperplane sections of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ be the du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces defined by~\textup{\eqref{eq:cx-p1p1p1}}. Then \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{Z}}_2 = S \sqcup S \sqcup S, \qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_3 = S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {{\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}}, \end{equation*} and the Brauer classes $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ and $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ are both trivial.
nodes.statement_short: For hyperplane sections of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^3$, $\mathscr{Z}_2 = S\sqcup S\sqcup S$, $\mathscr{Z}_3$ is the double cover branched over the Cayley quartic, and both Brauer classes vanish.
assumptions: Let ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ be the du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces defined by~\textup{\eqref{eq:cx-p1p1p1}}.
conclusions: Then \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{Z}}_2 = S \sqcup S \sqcup S, \qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_3 = S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {{\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}}, \end{equation*} and the Brauer classes $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ and $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ are both trivial.
nodes.label: proposition:dp-p1p1p1

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.6
nodes.statement: The proof is parallel to that of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dp-p2p2}. Using homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)$, see Theorem~\ref{theorem:hpd-p1p1p1}, we obtain from~\cite[Theorem~6.27]{kuznetsov2007hpd} a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_3}({\mathbf{D}}(S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3)), \\ {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(1,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(1,2,1), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(1,1,2) \rangle, \end{multline*} where ${\mathbb{Y}}_3 \to {\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}$ is the resolution of singularities defined in~\eqref{eq:def-yy3} and where ${\mathscr{E}}_3$ is the derived pullback of the sheaf ${\mathbb{E}}_3$ defined by~\eqref{eq:hpd-kernel-xxx3} with respect to the natural map \begin{equation} {\mathscr{X}} \times_S (S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3) \to {\mathscr{X}}_3 \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3 \end{equation} (we will discuss this map below). Mutating the last four components to the far left (again, note that~\mbox{$K_{\mathscr{X}} = {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(-1,-1,-1)$} in the relative Picard group~$\mathrm{Pic}({\mathscr{X}}/S)$), we get \begin{multline} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}, {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(1,0,0), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(0,1,0), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(0,0,1), \\ \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_3}({\mathbf{D}}(S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3)) \rangle. \end{multline} We claim that this decomposition agrees with the general decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbcx-again} for a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces. Indeed, its second, third and fourth components can be considered as the derived category of $S \sqcup S \sqcup S$ (the trivial triple covering of $S$) embedded via the Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{E}}_2 := {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(1,0,0) \sqcup {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(0,1,0) \sqcup {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(0,0,1) \in {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}} \sqcup {\mathscr{X}} \sqcup {\mathscr{X}}) = {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}} \times_S (S \sqcup S \sqcup S)), \end{equation*} while the last component is the derived category of~$S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3 = S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {{\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}}$ (recall that ${\mathbb{Y}}_3$ maps birationally onto ${{\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}}$ and $S$ by definition does not touch the image $\overline{\mathrm{O}}_4$ (see Remark~\ref{remark:fibers-resolution-dvvv}) of the indeterminacy locus of that birational isomorphism), which is a flat degree~2 covering of~$S$ (since ${{\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}}$ is flat over the complement of~$\overline{\mathrm{O}}_4$), and it is embedded into~${\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$ via the Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel~${\mathscr{E}}_3$. Let us check that both ${\mathscr{E}}_2$ and ${\mathscr{E}}_3$ are flat families of torsion-free rank 1 sheaves on the fibers of ${\mathscr{X}}$ over~$S$ with Hilbert polynomials $h_2(t)$ and $h_3(t)$ respectively, parameterized by \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{Z}}'_2 := S \sqcup S \sqcup S \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{Z}}'_3 := S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3. \end{equation*} For the first flatness is clear and Hilbert polynomial computation is straightforward, so we skip it. For the second we note that the map~\eqref{eq:map-cx3} is flat. Indeed, arguing as in the proof of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dp-p2p2} we can check that the map~\eqref{eq:map-cx3} is obtained by base change from the map \begin{equation*} {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{L}}^\perp) \times_S {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{L}}) \to Q = \mathrm{Fl}(1,7;V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee) \end{equation*} which is an open embedding. Recall the embedding of the Weil divisor ${\mathbb{Y}}_3 \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3) \hookrightarrow {\mathscr{X}}_3 \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3$ defined by~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx}. The preimage of ${\mathbb{Y}}_3 \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)$ under~\eqref{eq:map-cx3} is a Weil divisor in ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S (S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3)$ such that for any closed point $(b,v_1,v_2)$ of ${\mathscr{Z}}'_3 = S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3$ its fiber is the Weil divisor \begin{equation*} L := X_b \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)} \{(v_1,v_2)\} \subset X_b, \end{equation*} i.e., a line on the sextic del Pezzo surface $X_b$ contracted by the projection $X_b \to {\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)$ to the point $(v_1,v_2) \in {\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)$. Thus, by~\eqref{eq:hpd-kernel-xxx3}, the sheaf we are interested in is the twisted ideal \mbox{${\mathscr{I}}_L \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1)$}. In particular, it is torsion-free, and its Hilbert polynomial equals~$h_3(t)$. The rest of the proof repeats the argument of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dp-p2p2}.
nodes.statement_short: Parallel to Proposition 6.2: HPD for (P^1)^3 (Theorem D.1) gives a decomposition; the HPD kernels are flat families of rank-1 sheaves with polynomials h_2, h_3, identifying Z_2, Z_3.

nodes.name: Parallel to Proposition 6.2
nodes.statement: The proof is parallel to that of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dp-p2p2}.
nodes.statement_short: Parallel to Proposition 6.2

nodes.name: Decomposition from HPD (Theorem D.1)
nodes.statement: Using homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)$, see Theorem~\ref{theorem:hpd-p1p1p1}, we obtain from~\cite[Theorem~6.27]{kuznetsov2007hpd} a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_3}({\mathbf{D}}(S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3)), \\ {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(1,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(1,2,1), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(1,1,2) \rangle, \end{multline*} where ${\mathbb{Y}}_3 \to {\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}$ is the resolution of singularities defined in~\eqref{eq:def-yy3} and where ${\mathscr{E}}_3$ is the derived pullback of the sheaf ${\mathbb{E}}_3$ defined by~\eqref{eq:hpd-kernel-xxx3} with respect to the natural map \begin{equation} {\mathscr{X}} \times_S (S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3) \to {\mathscr{X}}_3 \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3 \end{equation} (we will discuss this map below).
nodes.statement_short: Decomposition from HPD (Theorem D.1)

nodes.name: Natural map for the (P^1)^3 family
nodes.statement: {\mathscr{X}} \times_S (S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3) \to {\mathscr{X}}_3 \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3
nodes.label: eq:map-cx3

nodes.name: Mutate to the standard form
nodes.statement: Mutating the last four components to the far left (again, note that~\mbox{$K_{\mathscr{X}} = {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(-1,-1,-1)$} in the relative Picard group~$\mathrm{Pic}({\mathscr{X}}/S)$), we get \begin{multline} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}, {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(1,0,0), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(0,1,0), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(0,0,1), \\ \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_3}({\mathbf{D}}(S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3)) \rangle. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Mutate to the standard form

nodes.name: Mutated decomposition for the (P^1)^3 family
nodes.statement: {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}, {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(1,0,0), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(0,1,0), {\mathbf{D}}(S) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(0,0,1), \\ \Phi_{{\mathscr{E}}_3}({\mathbf{D}}(S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3)) \rangle.

nodes.name: Match components with S + S + S and the double cover
nodes.statement: We claim that this decomposition agrees with the general decomposition~\eqref{eq:dbcx-again} for a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces. Indeed, its second, third and fourth components can be considered as the derived category of $S \sqcup S \sqcup S$ (the trivial triple covering of $S$) embedded via the Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{E}}_2 := {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(1,0,0) \sqcup {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(0,1,0) \sqcup {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathscr{X}}(0,0,1) \in {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}} \sqcup {\mathscr{X}} \sqcup {\mathscr{X}}) = {\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}} \times_S (S \sqcup S \sqcup S)), \end{equation*} while the last component is the derived category of~$S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3 = S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {{\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}}$ (recall that ${\mathbb{Y}}_3$ maps birationally onto ${{\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}}$ and $S$ by definition does not touch the image $\overline{\mathrm{O}}_4$ (see Remark~\ref{remark:fibers-resolution-dvvv}) of the indeterminacy locus of that birational isomorphism), which is a flat degree~2 covering of~$S$ (since ${{\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}}$ is flat over the complement of~$\overline{\mathrm{O}}_4$), and it is embedded into~${\mathbf{D}}({\mathscr{X}})$ via the Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel~${\mathscr{E}}_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Match components with S + S + S and the double cover

nodes.name: Kernels are flat families
nodes.statement: Let us check that both ${\mathscr{E}}_2$ and ${\mathscr{E}}_3$ are flat families of torsion-free rank 1 sheaves on the fibers of ${\mathscr{X}}$ over~$S$ with Hilbert polynomials $h_2(t)$ and $h_3(t)$ respectively, parameterized by \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{Z}}'_2 := S \sqcup S \sqcup S \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{Z}}'_3 := S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3. \end{equation*} For the first flatness is clear and Hilbert polynomial computation is straightforward, so we skip it. For the second we note that the map~\eqref{eq:map-cx3} is flat. Indeed, arguing as in the proof of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dp-p2p2} we can check that the map~\eqref{eq:map-cx3} is obtained by base change from the map \begin{equation*} {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{L}}^\perp) \times_S {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{L}}) \to Q = \mathrm{Fl}(1,7;V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee) \end{equation*} which is an open embedding.
nodes.statement_short: Kernels are flat families

nodes.name: First family clear; second reduces to flatness of the map
nodes.statement: For the first flatness is clear and Hilbert polynomial computation is straightforward, so we skip it. For the second we note that the map~\eqref{eq:map-cx3} is flat.
nodes.statement_short: First family clear; second reduces to flatness of the map

nodes.name: Map obtained by base change from an open embedding
nodes.statement: Indeed, arguing as in the proof of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dp-p2p2} we can check that the map~\eqref{eq:map-cx3} is obtained by base change from the map \begin{equation*} {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{L}}^\perp) \times_S {\mathbb{P}}_S({\mathscr{L}}) \to Q = \mathrm{Fl}(1,7;V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee) \end{equation*} which is an open embedding.
nodes.statement_short: Map obtained by base change from an open embedding

nodes.name: Recall the Weil divisor
nodes.statement: Recall the embedding of the Weil divisor ${\mathbb{Y}}_3 \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3) \hookrightarrow {\mathscr{X}}_3 \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3$ defined by~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the Weil divisor

nodes.name: Fibers are twisted ideal sheaves of lines; polynomial h_3
nodes.statement: The preimage of ${\mathbb{Y}}_3 \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)$ under~\eqref{eq:map-cx3} is a Weil divisor in ${\mathscr{X}} \times_S (S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3)$ such that for any closed point $(b,v_1,v_2)$ of ${\mathscr{Z}}'_3 = S \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1^\vee \otimes V_2^\vee \otimes V_3^\vee)} {\mathbb{Y}}_3$ its fiber is the Weil divisor \begin{equation*} L := X_b \times_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)} \{(v_1,v_2)\} \subset X_b, \end{equation*} i.e., a line on the sextic del Pezzo surface $X_b$ contracted by the projection $X_b \to {\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)$ to the point $(v_1,v_2) \in {\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)$. Thus, by~\eqref{eq:hpd-kernel-xxx3}, the sheaf we are interested in is the twisted ideal \mbox{${\mathscr{I}}_L \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1)$}. In particular, it is torsion-free, and its Hilbert polynomial equals~$h_3(t)$.
nodes.statement_short: Fibers are twisted ideal sheaves of lines; polynomial h_3

nodes.name: Conclude as in Proposition 6.2
nodes.statement: The rest of the proof repeats the argument of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dp-p2p2}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude as in Proposition 6.2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.7 (by reference)
nodes.statement: The statement of Proposition~\ref{proposition:dp-p1p1p1} can be inverted as follows (and the proof repeats the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma:reconstructing-family}).
nodes.statement_short: The proof repeats that of Lemma 6.4.

nodes.name: Reconstructing a family from $\mathscr{Z}_2 = S\sqcup S\sqcup S$
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ be a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces. If ${\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S) = S \sqcup S \sqcup S$ and the Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ is trivial, then Zariski locally over $S$ the family ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ can be represented as a family of hyperplane sections of\/ ${\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1$. In particular, if ${\mathscr{X}}$ is regular then $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ is trivial.
nodes.statement_short: If $\mathscr{Z}_2 = S\sqcup S\sqcup S$ with trivial Brauer class, the family is locally a family of hyperplane sections of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^3$.
assumptions: Let ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ be a du Val family of sextic del Pezzo surfaces.
If ${\mathscr{Z}}_2({\mathscr{X}}/S) = S \sqcup S \sqcup S$ and the Brauer class $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ is trivial,
conclusions: then Zariski locally over $S$ the family ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ can be represented as a family of hyperplane sections of\/ ${\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1$.
In particular, if ${\mathscr{X}}$ is regular then $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ is trivial.

nodes.name: Blowup $\widehat{X}$ of a length 3 subscheme
nodes.statement: For each length 3 subscheme $Y \subset {\mathbb{P}}^2$, consider the blowup \begin{equation*} \widehat{X} := \mathrm{Bl}_Y({\mathbb{P}}^2). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Blowups of length 3 subschemes are weak del Pezzo
nodes.statement: Unless $Y$ is the infinitesimal neighborhood of a point (i.e., is given by the square of the maximal ideal of a point), $\widehat{X}$ is a weak del Pezzo surface of degree 6. In particular, the anticanonical class of $\widehat{X}$ is nef and big and the anticanonical model of $\widehat{X}$ (i.e., the image of $\widehat{X}$ under the anticanonical map) is a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface.

nodes.name: Base $S = (\mathbb{P}^2)^{[3]}\setminus\mathbb{P}^2$
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation} S := ({\mathbb{P}}^2)^{[3]} \setminus {\mathbb{P}}^2 \end{equation} be the open subset of the Hilbert cube of the plane parameterizing length 3 subschemes in ${\mathbb{P}}^2$ avoiding infinitesimal neighborhoods of points.

nodes.name: Base $S$ of the blowup family
nodes.statement: S := ({\mathbb{P}}^2)^{[3]} \setminus {\mathbb{P}}^2
nodes.label: eq:hilb-p2

nodes.name: Universal family $\mathscr{Y}$ of length 3 subschemes
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathscr{Y}} \subset {\mathbb{P}}^2 \times S$ be the corresponding family of subschemes.

nodes.name: Blowup family $\widehat{\mathscr{X}}$ and its anticanonical model
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation*} {\widehat{{\mathscr{X}}}} := \mathrm{Bl}_{\mathscr{Y}}({\mathbb{P}}^2 \times S) \end{equation*} be the blowup and ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ its relative anticanonical model.

nodes.name: Divisor $S_1$ of collinear subschemes
nodes.statement: Let $S_1 \subset S$ be the divisor parameterizing subschemes in ${\mathbb{P}}^2$ contained in a line.

nodes.name: Blowup family of $\mathbb{P}^2$
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be defined by~\eqref{eq:hilb-p2} and let ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ be the relative anticanonical model of the blowup ${\widehat{{\mathscr{X}}}} = \mathrm{Bl}_{\mathscr{Y}}({\mathbb{P}}^2 \times S) \to S$. Then \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{Z}}_2 \cong {\mathscr{Y}} \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_3 \cong S \,\mathop\cup\limits_{S_1}\, S, \end{equation*} and both Brauer classes $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ and $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ are trivial.
nodes.statement_short: For blowups of $\mathbb{P}^2$ in length-3 subschemes, $\mathscr{Z}_2\cong\mathscr{Y}$, $\mathscr{Z}_3$ is two copies of S glued along $S_1$, and both Brauer classes vanish.
assumptions: Let $S$ be defined by~\eqref{eq:hilb-p2} and let ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ be the relative anticanonical model of the blowup ${\widehat{{\mathscr{X}}}} = \mathrm{Bl}_{\mathscr{Y}}({\mathbb{P}}^2 \times S) \to S$.
conclusions: Then \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{Z}}_2 \cong {\mathscr{Y}} \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_3 \cong S \,\mathop\cup\limits_{S_1}\, S, \end{equation*} and both Brauer classes $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ and $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ are trivial.
nodes.label: proposition:blowup-p2

nodes.name: Gluing $S \cup_{S_1} S$
nodes.statement: Here $S \,\mathop\cup\limits_{S_1}\, S$ is the gluing of two copies of the scheme $S$ along the divisor~$S_1$.

nodes.name: Non-regularity in the blowup family
nodes.statement: In particular, in this example both ${\mathscr{X}}$ and ${\mathscr{Z}}_3$ are not regular.

nodes.name: Blowup family of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$
nodes.statement: Let $S := ({\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1)^{[2]}$ be the Hilbert square of ${\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1$ and let ${\mathscr{Y}} \subset ({\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1) \times S$ be the universal family of subschemes. Let ${\widehat{{\mathscr{X}}}} := \mathrm{Bl}_{{\mathscr{Y}}}({\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1 \times S)$ be the blowup and let ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ be its relative anticanonical model. Let $S_{1,0} \subset S$ and $S_{0,1} \subset S$ be the divisors parameterizing subschemes contained in a horizontal or a vertical ruling of ${\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1$ respectively. Then \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{Z}}_2 \cong S \,\mathop\cup\limits_{S_{1,0}}\, S \,\mathop\cup\limits_{S_{0,1}}\, S \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_3 \cong {\mathscr{Y}} \end{equation*} and both Brauer classes $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ and $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ are trivial.
nodes.statement_short: For blowups of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ in length-2 subschemes, $\mathscr{Z}_2$ is three copies of S glued along two divisors, $\mathscr{Z}_3\cong\mathscr{Y}$, with trivial Brauer classes.
assumptions: Let $S := ({\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1)^{[2]}$ be the Hilbert square of ${\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1$ and let ${\mathscr{Y}} \subset ({\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1) \times S$ be the universal family of subschemes. Let ${\widehat{{\mathscr{X}}}} := \mathrm{Bl}_{{\mathscr{Y}}}({\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1 \times S)$ be the blowup and let ${\mathscr{X}} \to S$ be its relative anticanonical model. Let $S_{1,0} \subset S$ and $S_{0,1} \subset S$ be the divisors parameterizing subschemes contained in a horizontal or a vertical ruling of ${\mathbb{P}}^1 \times {\mathbb{P}}^1$ respectively.
conclusions: Then \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{Z}}_2 \cong S \,\mathop\cup\limits_{S_{1,0}}\, S \,\mathop\cup\limits_{S_{0,1}}\, S \qquad\text{and}\qquad {\mathscr{Z}}_3 \cong {\mathscr{Y}} \end{equation*} and both Brauer classes $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_2}$ and $\beta_{{\mathscr{Z}}_3}$ are trivial.
nodes.label: proposition:blowup-p1p1

nodes.name: Auslander algebra as a categorical resolution
nodes.statement: The Auslander algebra ${\tilde{R}}_m$ defined below provides a categorical resolution of the derived category ${\mathbf{D}}(Z)$, see~\cite[Section~5]{kuznetsov2015categorical} for details.

nodes.name: Auslander algebra $\tilde{R}_m$
nodes.statement: The algebra ${\tilde{R}}_m$ is defined as the path algebra of a quiver with relations: \begin{equation} {\tilde{R}}_m = {\mathsf{k}}\left\{\left. \xymatrix@1{\bullet \ar@<-.5ex>[r]_-{\beta_1} & \bullet \ar@<-.5ex>[l]_-{\alpha_1} \ar@<-.5ex>[r]_-{\beta_2} & \bullet \ar@<-.5ex>[l]_-{\alpha_2} \ar@{}[r]|-{\dots} & \bullet \ar@<-.5ex>[r]_-{\beta_{m-1}} & \bullet \ar@<-.5ex>[l]_-{\alpha_{m-1}} } \ \right|\ \text{$\beta_i\alpha_i = \alpha_{i+1}\beta_{i+1}$ for $1 \le i \le m-2$, $\beta_{m-1}\alpha_{m-1} = 0$}\ \right\}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde R_m$ is the path algebra of the $A_m$ double quiver with relations $\beta_i\alpha_i=\alpha_{i+1}\beta_{i+1}$, $\beta_{m-1}\alpha_{m-1}=0$.
nodes.genus: path algebra of a quiver with relations

nodes.name: Quiver presentation of $\tilde{R}_m$
nodes.statement: {\tilde{R}}_m = {\mathsf{k}}\left\{\left. \xymatrix@1{\bullet \ar@<-.5ex>[r]_-{\beta_1} & \bullet \ar@<-.5ex>[l]_-{\alpha_1} \ar@<-.5ex>[r]_-{\beta_2} & \bullet \ar@<-.5ex>[l]_-{\alpha_2} \ar@{}[r]|-{\dots} & \bullet \ar@<-.5ex>[r]_-{\beta_{m-1}} & \bullet \ar@<-.5ex>[l]_-{\alpha_{m-1}} } \ \right|\ \text{$\beta_i\alpha_i = \alpha_{i+1}\beta_{i+1}$ for $1 \le i \le m-2$, $\beta_{m-1}\alpha_{m-1} = 0$}\ \right\}.
nodes.label: eq:trm

nodes.name: Matrix presentation of $\tilde{R}_m$
nodes.statement: Alternatively, it can be written as a matrix algebra \begin{equation} {\tilde{R}}_m = \bigoplus_{i,j = 0}^{m-1} ({\tilde{R}}_m)_{ij}, \qquad ({\tilde{R}}_m)_{ij} = \begin{cases} {\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^{m-i}, & \text{if $i \ge j$},\\ t^{j-i}{\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^{m-i}, & \text{if $i \le j$}, \end{cases} \end{equation} with multiplication induced by the natural maps $({\tilde{R}}_m)_{ij} \otimes ({\tilde{R}}_m)_{jk} \to ({\tilde{R}}_m)_{ik}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde R_m$ is the matrix algebra with entries $\mathsf{k}[t]/t^{m-i}$ or $t^{j-i}\mathsf{k}[t]/t^{m-i}$.

nodes.name: Matrix presentation of $\tilde{R}_m$
nodes.statement: {\tilde{R}}_m = \bigoplus_{i,j = 0}^{m-1} ({\tilde{R}}_m)_{ij}, \qquad ({\tilde{R}}_m)_{ij} = \begin{cases} {\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^{m-i}, & \text{if $i \ge j$},\\ t^{j-i}{\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^{m-i}, & \text{if $i \le j$}, \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq:trm-matrix

nodes.name: Vertex idempotents $\epsilon_i$
nodes.statement: We denote by $\epsilon_i$ the $i$-th vertex idempotent in ${\tilde{R}}_m$ (in terms of~\eqref{eq:trm-matrix} it is the unit in $({\tilde{R}}_m)_{ii} \cong {\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^{m-i}$).

nodes.name: Components and dimension vector of a module
nodes.statement: We call $M_i := \epsilon_i M$ the {\sf $i$-th component} of $M$, and the vector $(\dim M_0,\dim M_1, \dots) \in {\mathbb{Z}}^m$ the {\sf dimension vector} of $M$.

nodes.name: Simple modules $S_i$ and projective modules $P_i$
nodes.statement: For each $0 \le i \le m-1$ we denote by $S_i$ the {\sf simple module} of $i$-th vertex of the quiver (its dimension vector is $(\underbrace{0, \dots, 0}_{i},1,\underbrace{0,\dots, 0}_{m-1-i})$) and by \begin{equation*} P_i = {\tilde{R}}_m \epsilon_i \end{equation*} its indecomposable projective cover ({\sf projective module} of $i$-th vertex).

nodes.name: Exceptional modules $E_i$
nodes.statement: The algebra ${\tilde{R}}_m$ has finite global dimension (it is bounded by $2m - 2$, see~\cite[Proposition~A.14]{kuznetsov2015categorical}) and its derived category ${\mathbf{D}}({\tilde{R}}_m)$ is generated by an exceptional collection (see Lemma~\ref{lemma:auslander-ext-ei}) consisting of representations~$E_i$ with dimension vectors \begin{equation*} \dim(E_i) = (\underbrace{1,\dots,1}_{i+1},\underbrace{0,\dots,0}_{m-1-i}) \end{equation*} and with $\beta$-arrows acting by zero and $\alpha$-arrows acting by identity.
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde R_m$ has finite global dimension and $\mathbf{D}(\tilde R_m)$ is generated by the exceptional representations $E_i$ with dimension vector (1,...,1,0,...,0).

nodes.name: Quasi-hereditary structure
nodes.statement: Actually, the algebra ${\tilde{R}}_m$ is quasihereditary and the modules $E_i$ are its standard modules.
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde R_m$ is quasihereditary with standard modules $E_i$.

nodes.name: Standard exceptional modules
nodes.statement: We call the $E_i$ {\sf standard exceptional modules}.

nodes.name: Projective resolutions of $E_i$
nodes.statement: 0 \to P_{i+1} \xrightarrow{\ \beta_{i+1}\ } P_i \to E_i \to 0,
nodes.label: eq:projective-resolution-ei

nodes.name: Ext-algebra of the standard exceptional modules
nodes.statement: The collection $E_0,E_1,\dots,E_{m-1}$ is exceptional and $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,E_j) = {\mathsf{k}} \oplus {\mathsf{k}}[-1]$ for all $i < j$. Moreover, the multiplication map \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^p(E_i,E_j) \otimes \mathrm{Ext}^q(E_j,E_k) \to \mathrm{Ext}^{p+q}(E_i,E_k), \qquad i < j < k \end{equation*} is an isomorphism when $p = 0$ or $q = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: $E_0,\dots,E_{m-1}$ is exceptional with $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,E_j)=\mathsf{k}\oplus\mathsf{k}[-1]$ for $i<j$, and multiplication is an isomorphism when one degree is 0.
conclusions: The collection $E_0,E_1,\dots,E_{m-1}$ is exceptional and $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,E_j) = {\mathsf{k}} \oplus {\mathsf{k}}[-1]$ for all $i < j$.

Moreover, the multiplication map \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^p(E_i,E_j) \otimes \mathrm{Ext}^q(E_j,E_k) \to \mathrm{Ext}^{p+q}(E_i,E_k), \qquad i < j < k \end{equation*} is an isomorphism when $p = 0$ or $q = 0$.
nodes.label: lemma:auslander-ext-ei

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.2
nodes.statement: Using~\eqref{eq:projective-resolution-ei} we see that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,E_j)$ is computed by the complex \begin{equation*} (E_j)_i \xrightarrow{\ \beta_{i+1}\ } (E_j)_{i+1}. \end{equation*} If $i > j$ both spaces are zero and if $i = j$ the first is ${\mathsf{k}}$ and the second is zero, hence the collection is exceptional. Similarly, if $j > i$ both spaces are ${\mathsf{k}}$ and the arrow is zero, hence $\mathrm{Hom}(E_i,E_j) = \mathrm{Ext}^1(E_i,E_j) = {\mathsf{k}}$. For the second statement, note that we have an exact sequence \begin{equation} 0 \to E_{i-1} \xrightarrow{\ \alpha_i\ } E_i \to S_i \to 0, \end{equation} which shows that for $j \le k$ the natural map $E_j \to E_k$ is injective and its cokernel is an extension of simple modules $S_l$ with $j+1 \le l \le k$. On the other hand, \eqref{eq:projective-resolution-ei} implies that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,S_l) = 0$ as soon as~$l \ge i+2$, hence the map \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,E_j) \to \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,E_k) \end{equation*} induced by the embedding $E_j \to E_k$ is an isomorphism. This proves the case when $q = 0$. Similarly, merging~\eqref{eq:resolution-simple} with~\eqref{eq:projective-resolution-ei} we obtain for $l \ge 1$ a projective resolution \begin{equation} 0 \to P_l \xrightarrow{\ (-\alpha_{l+1},\beta_l)\ } P_{l+1} \oplus P_{l-1} \xrightarrow{\ (\beta_{l+1},\alpha_l)\ } P_l \to S_l \to 0 \end{equation} of the simple module $S_l$. It follows that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(S_l,E_k)$ for $1 \le l < k$ are computed by the complex \begin{equation*} (E_k)_l \xrightarrow{\ (0,1)\ } (E_k)_{l+1} \oplus (E_k)_{l-1} \xrightarrow{\ (-1,0)} (E_k)_l, \end{equation*} hence for $1 \le l < k$ we have $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(S_l,E_k) = 0$. On the other hand, the cokernel of the embedding $E_i \to E_j$ is an extension of simple modules $S_l$ with $1 \le l \le j$, hence the map \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_j,E_k) \to \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,E_k) \end{equation*} induced by this embedding is an isomorphism. This proves the case when $p = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute Ext via the two-term projective resolutions; for multiplication, use that cokernels of E_j -> E_k are built from simples that are Ext-orthogonal to the relevant E_i.

nodes.name: Ext computed by a two-term complex
nodes.statement: Using~\eqref{eq:projective-resolution-ei} we see that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,E_j)$ is computed by the complex \begin{equation*} (E_j)_i \xrightarrow{\ \beta_{i+1}\ } (E_j)_{i+1}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Ext computed by a two-term complex

nodes.name: Exceptionality and Ext for i < j
nodes.statement: If $i > j$ both spaces are zero and if $i = j$ the first is ${\mathsf{k}}$ and the second is zero, hence the collection is exceptional. Similarly, if $j > i$ both spaces are ${\mathsf{k}}$ and the arrow is zero, hence $\mathrm{Hom}(E_i,E_j) = \mathrm{Ext}^1(E_i,E_j) = {\mathsf{k}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Exceptionality and Ext for i < j

nodes.name: Cokernels built from simples
nodes.statement: For the second statement, note that we have an exact sequence \begin{equation} 0 \to E_{i-1} \xrightarrow{\ \alpha_i\ } E_i \to S_i \to 0, \end{equation} which shows that for $j \le k$ the natural map $E_j \to E_k$ is injective and its cokernel is an extension of simple modules $S_l$ with $j+1 \le l \le k$.
nodes.statement_short: Cokernels built from simples

nodes.name: Exact sequence $E_{i-1}\to E_i\to S_i$
nodes.statement: 0 \to E_{i-1} \xrightarrow{\ \alpha_i\ } E_i \to S_i \to 0,
nodes.label: eq:resolution-simple

nodes.name: Case q = 0
nodes.statement: On the other hand, \eqref{eq:projective-resolution-ei} implies that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,S_l) = 0$ as soon as~$l \ge i+2$, hence the map \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,E_j) \to \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,E_k) \end{equation*} induced by the embedding $E_j \to E_k$ is an isomorphism. This proves the case when $q = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Case q = 0

nodes.name: Projective resolution of simples
nodes.statement: Similarly, merging~\eqref{eq:resolution-simple} with~\eqref{eq:projective-resolution-ei} we obtain for $l \ge 1$ a projective resolution \begin{equation} 0 \to P_l \xrightarrow{\ (-\alpha_{l+1},\beta_l)\ } P_{l+1} \oplus P_{l-1} \xrightarrow{\ (\beta_{l+1},\alpha_l)\ } P_l \to S_l \to 0 \end{equation} of the simple module $S_l$.
nodes.statement_short: Projective resolution of simples

nodes.name: Projective resolution of simple modules
nodes.statement: 0 \to P_l \xrightarrow{\ (-\alpha_{l+1},\beta_l)\ } P_{l+1} \oplus P_{l-1} \xrightarrow{\ (\beta_{l+1},\alpha_l)\ } P_l \to S_l \to 0
nodes.label: eq:projective-resolution-simples

nodes.name: Ext(S_l, E_k) = 0 for 1 <= l < k
nodes.statement: It follows that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(S_l,E_k)$ for $1 \le l < k$ are computed by the complex \begin{equation*} (E_k)_l \xrightarrow{\ (0,1)\ } (E_k)_{l+1} \oplus (E_k)_{l-1} \xrightarrow{\ (-1,0)} (E_k)_l, \end{equation*} hence for $1 \le l < k$ we have $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(S_l,E_k) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Ext(S_l, E_k) = 0 for 1 <= l < k

nodes.name: Case p = 0
nodes.statement: On the other hand, the cokernel of the embedding $E_i \to E_j$ is an extension of simple modules $S_l$ with $1 \le l \le j$, hence the map \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_j,E_k) \to \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet(E_i,E_k) \end{equation*} induced by this embedding is an isomorphism. This proves the case when $p = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Case p = 0

nodes.name: Recognizing $\mathbf{D}(\tilde{R}_2)$ and $\mathbf{D}(\tilde{R}_3)$
nodes.statement: Assume ${\mathscr{T}}$ is a triangulated category admitting a DG enhancement. \noindent$(a)$ If ${\mathscr{T}}$ is generated by an exceptional pair $({\mathscr{L}}_0,{\mathscr{L}}_1)$ such that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{L}}_0,{\mathscr{L}}_1) \cong {\mathsf{k}} \oplus {\mathsf{k}}[-1]$ then there is an equivalence of categories ${\mathscr{T}} \cong {\mathbf{D}}({\tilde{R}}_2)$ taking ${\mathscr{L}}_i$ to $E_i$. \noindent$(b)$ If ${\mathscr{T}}$ is generated by an exceptional triple $({\mathscr{L}}_0,{\mathscr{L}}_1,{\mathscr{L}}_2)$ such that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{L}}_i,{\mathscr{L}}_j) \cong {\mathsf{k}} \oplus {\mathsf{k}}[-1]$ for all~\mbox{$i < j$} and the multiplication map $\mathrm{Ext}^p({\mathscr{L}}_0,{\mathscr{L}}_1) \otimes \mathrm{Ext}^q({\mathscr{L}}_1,{\mathscr{L}}_2) \to \mathrm{Ext}^{p+q}({\mathscr{L}}_0,{\mathscr{L}}_2)$ is an isomorphism when $p = 0$ or $q = 0$, then there is an equivalence of categories ${\mathscr{T}} \cong {\mathbf{D}}({\tilde{R}}_3)$ taking ${\mathscr{L}}_i$ to $E_i$.
nodes.statement_short: An enhanced category generated by an exceptional pair or triple with the Ext-pattern of Lemma A.2 is equivalent to $\mathbf{D}(\tilde R_2)$ or $\mathbf{D}(\tilde R_3)$.
assumptions: Assume ${\mathscr{T}}$ is a triangulated category admitting a DG enhancement.
conclusions: If ${\mathscr{T}}$ is generated by an exceptional pair $({\mathscr{L}}_0,{\mathscr{L}}_1)$ such that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{L}}_0,{\mathscr{L}}_1) \cong {\mathsf{k}} \oplus {\mathsf{k}}[-1]$ then there is an equivalence of categories ${\mathscr{T}} \cong {\mathbf{D}}({\tilde{R}}_2)$ taking ${\mathscr{L}}_i$ to $E_i$.

If ${\mathscr{T}}$ is generated by an exceptional triple $({\mathscr{L}}_0,{\mathscr{L}}_1,{\mathscr{L}}_2)$ such that $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet({\mathscr{L}}_i,{\mathscr{L}}_j) \cong {\mathsf{k}} \oplus {\mathsf{k}}[-1]$ for all~\mbox{$i < j$} and the multiplication map $\mathrm{Ext}^p({\mathscr{L}}_0,{\mathscr{L}}_1) \otimes \mathrm{Ext}^q({\mathscr{L}}_1,{\mathscr{L}}_2) \to \mathrm{Ext}^{p+q}({\mathscr{L}}_0,{\mathscr{L}}_2)$ is an isomorphism when $p = 0$ or $q = 0$, then there is an equivalence of categories ${\mathscr{T}} \cong {\mathbf{D}}({\tilde{R}}_3)$ taking ${\mathscr{L}}_i$ to $E_i$.
nodes.label: proposition:rm-equivalence

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition A.3
nodes.statement: Since the category ${\mathscr{T}}$ is enhanced, there is an equivalence of ${\mathscr{T}}$ with the derived category of the DG algebra $\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathscr{T}}(\oplus {\mathscr{L}}_i,\oplus {\mathscr{L}}_i)$. By the assumption, its cohomology is isomorphic (as a graded algebra) to the graded algebra $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet_{{\mathbf{D}}({\tilde{R}}_m)}(\oplus E_i, \oplus E_i)$. To get the desired equivalence, it remains to check that the latter algebra (considered as a DG algebra with trivial differential) is formal. But formality is clear, since any higher $A_\infty$-operation ${\mathbf{m}}_i$ (with $i \ge 3$) requires at least three non-trivial arguments, so one needs the quiver to have at least four vertices to admit such an operation. So, for ${\tilde{R}}_2$ and ${\tilde{R}}_3$ all higher operations vanish and the algebra is formal.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to formality of the Ext-algebra; higher A-infinity operations need at least four vertices, so they vanish for two or three.

nodes.name: Equivalence with DG modules over the endomorphism DG algebra
nodes.statement: Since the category ${\mathscr{T}}$ is enhanced, there is an equivalence of ${\mathscr{T}}$ with the derived category of the DG algebra $\mathrm{RHom}_{\mathscr{T}}(\oplus {\mathscr{L}}_i,\oplus {\mathscr{L}}_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: Equivalence with DG modules over the endomorphism DG algebra

nodes.name: Cohomology algebras agree
nodes.statement: By the assumption, its cohomology is isomorphic (as a graded algebra) to the graded algebra $\mathrm{Ext}^\bullet_{{\mathbf{D}}({\tilde{R}}_m)}(\oplus E_i, \oplus E_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: Cohomology algebras agree

nodes.name: Remains: formality
nodes.statement: To get the desired equivalence, it remains to check that the latter algebra (considered as a DG algebra with trivial differential) is formal. But formality is clear, since any higher $A_\infty$-operation ${\mathbf{m}}_i$ (with $i \ge 3$) requires at least three non-trivial arguments, so one needs the quiver to have at least four vertices to admit such an operation.
nodes.statement_short: Remains: formality

nodes.name: Formality for two or three vertices
nodes.statement: So, for ${\tilde{R}}_2$ and ${\tilde{R}}_3$ all higher operations vanish and the algebra is formal.
nodes.statement_short: Formality for two or three vertices

nodes.name: The case $m \ge 4$
nodes.statement: Let $m \ge 4$ and assume ${\mathscr{T}}$ is an enhanced triangulated category generated by an exceptional collection ${\mathscr{L}}_0,{\mathscr{L}}_1,\dots,{\mathscr{L}}_{m-1}$ satisfying the properties of Lemma~\ref{lemma:auslander-ext-ei}. To establish an equivalence of ${\mathscr{T}}$ with~${\mathbf{D}}({\tilde{R}}_m)$ one should additionally check that higher $A_\infty$-operations in ${\mathscr{T}}$ vanish when one of the arguments is contained in the space $\mathrm{Hom}({\mathscr{L}}_i,{\mathscr{L}}_{i+1}) = {\mathsf{k}}$.
nodes.statement_short: For four or more objects one must additionally check vanishing of higher A-infinity operations.

nodes.name: Functors $\pi_{m*}$ and $\pi_m^*$
nodes.statement: Using this we define an adjoint pair of functors \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \pi_{m*} & \colon {\tilde{R}}_m\mathrm{-mod} \to ({\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m)\mathrm{-mod}, \quad & M & \mapsto \mathrm{Hom}_{{\tilde{R}}_m}(P_0,M) = \epsilon_0 M,\\ \pi_m^* & \colon ({\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m)\mathrm{-mod} \to {\tilde{R}}_m\mathrm{-mod}, \quad & N & \mapsto P_0 \otimes_{{\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m} N. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\pi_{m*}M = \epsilon_0 M$ and $\pi_m^*N = P_0\otimes N$ between $\tilde R_m$-modules and $\mathsf{k}[t]/t^m$-modules.

nodes.name: Definition of $\pi_{m*}$, $\pi_m^*$
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \pi_{m*} & \colon {\tilde{R}}_m\mathrm{-mod} \to ({\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m)\mathrm{-mod}, \quad & M & \mapsto \mathrm{Hom}_{{\tilde{R}}_m}(P_0,M) = \epsilon_0 M,\\ \pi_m^* & \colon ({\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m)\mathrm{-mod} \to {\tilde{R}}_m\mathrm{-mod}, \quad & N & \mapsto P_0 \otimes_{{\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m} N. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:pms

nodes.name: Localization $\pi_m^*$, $\pi_{m*}$
nodes.statement: The functor $\pi_m^* \colon {\mathbf{D}}^-({\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m) \to {\mathbf{D}}^-({\tilde{R}}_m)$ is fully faithful, and its right adjoint functor~$\pi_{m*} \colon {\mathbf{D}}({\tilde{R}}_m) \to {\mathbf{D}}({\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m)$ preserves boundedness and is essentially surjective. We have \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ker} \pi_{m*} = \langle S_1,\dots,S_{m-1} \rangle^\oplus \qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathrm{Im} \pi_m^* = \langle P_0 \rangle^\oplus = {}^\perp\langle S_1,\dots,S_{m-1} \rangle. \end{equation*} Moreover, $\pi_{m*}(S_0) = {\mathsf{k}}$ and $\pi_{m*}(P_0) = {\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m$.
nodes.statement_short: $\pi_m^*$ is fully faithful; $\pi_{m*}$ is essentially surjective, preserves boundedness, and its kernel is generated by $S_1,\dots,S_{m-1}$.
conclusions: The functor $\pi_m^* \colon {\mathbf{D}}^-({\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m) \to {\mathbf{D}}^-({\tilde{R}}_m)$ is fully faithful, and its right adjoint functor~$\pi_{m*} \colon {\mathbf{D}}({\tilde{R}}_m) \to {\mathbf{D}}({\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m)$ preserves boundedness and is essentially surjective.

We have \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ker} \pi_{m*} = \langle S_1,\dots,S_{m-1} \rangle^\oplus \qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathrm{Im} \pi_m^* = \langle P_0 \rangle^\oplus = {}^\perp\langle S_1,\dots,S_{m-1} \rangle. \end{equation*}
Moreover, $\pi_{m*}(S_0) = {\mathsf{k}}$ and $\pi_{m*}(P_0) = {\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m$.
nodes.label: proposition:auslander-localization

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition A.5
nodes.statement: The functor $\pi_m^*$ is fully faithful by~\cite[Theorem~5.23]{kuznetsov2015categorical} and $\pi_{m*} \circ \pi_m^* \cong \mathrm{id}$ by~\cite[(48)]{kuznetsov2015categorical}. Furthermore, $\pi_{m*}$ is exact by definition, hence for any $N \in {\mathbf{D}}({\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m)$, taking $M := \tau^{\ge p}\pi_m^*(N)$ (the canonical truncation) with $p \ll 0$, we obtain $N \cong \pi_{m_*}M$, hence $\pi_{m*}$ is essentially surjective. The image of~$\pi_m^*$ by definition equals the subcategory $\langle P_0 \rangle^\oplus \subset {\mathbf{D}}^-({\tilde{R}}_m)$ and this category is evidently equal to the orthogonal of the simple modules $S_1$, \dots, $S_{m-1}$. Since the functor $\pi_{m*}$ is the right adjoint of~$\pi_m^*$, we have $\mathrm{Ker} \pi_{m*} = (\mathrm{Im} \pi_m^*)^\perp = P_0^\perp = \langle S_1,\dots,S_{m-1} \rangle^\oplus$. Finally, applying~\eqref{eq:pms} we easily get~$\pi_{m*}(S_0) = \epsilon_0S_0 = {\mathsf{k}}$ and $\pi_{m*}(P_0) = \epsilon_0P_0 = \epsilon_0{\tilde{R}}_m\epsilon_0 = ({\tilde{R}}_m)_{00} = {\mathsf{k}}[t]/t^m$.

nodes.name: Moduli stack $\mathfrak{DP}_6$
nodes.statement: The moduli stack ${\mathfrak{DP}_6}$ of sextic du Val del Pezzo surfaces is the fibered category over $(\mathrm{Sch}/{\mathsf{k}})$ whose fiber over a ${\mathsf{k}}$-scheme $S$ is the groupoid of all du Val $S$-families of sextic del Pezzo surfaces $f \colon {\mathscr{X}} \to S$ (in the sense of Definition~\ref{definition:family-dp6}).
nodes.section: B Moduli stack of sextic du Val del Pezzo surfaces

nodes.name: Smoothness of the moduli stack of sextic du Val del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement: The moduli stack ${\mathfrak{DP}_6}$ is a smooth Artin stack of finite type over ${\mathsf{k}}$.
nodes.section: B Moduli stack of sextic du Val del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: The moduli stack of sextic du Val del Pezzo surfaces is a smooth Artin stack of finite type.
conclusions: The moduli stack ${\mathfrak{DP}_6}$ is a smooth Artin stack of finite type over ${\mathsf{k}}$.
nodes.label: theorem:moduli-stack-dp6

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem B.1
nodes.statement: By Hilbert scheme argument, the stack ${\mathfrak{DP}_6}$ is an Artin stack of finite type. So, by deformation theory it is enough to check that deformations of a sextic du Val del Pezzo surface $X$ over an algebraically closed field are unobstructed, i.e., that $\mathrm{Ext}^p(\Omega_X,{\mathscr{O}}_X) = 0$ for $p \ge 2$. On the other hand, since $X$ has isolated hypersurface singularities, the sheaf $\Omega_X$ has a locally free resolution of length~1, hence~$\mathscr{E}\mathit{xt}^p(\Omega_X,{\mathscr{O}}_X) = 0$ for $p \ge 2$ and $\mathscr{E}\mathit{xt}^1(\Omega_X,{\mathscr{O}}_X)$ has zero-dimensional support. By the local-to-global spectral sequence this means that \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Ext}^{\ge 2}(\Omega_X,{\mathscr{O}}_X) = H^{\ge 2}(X,T_X). \end{equation*} Since $X$ is a surface, we just have to check that $H^2(X,T_X) = 0$. This holds by~\cite[Proposition~3.1]{hacking2010smoothable}.
nodes.section: B Moduli stack of sextic du Val del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: Finite type by Hilbert schemes; unobstructedness reduces via the local-to-global spectral sequence to $H^2(X,T_X)=0$, cited from Hacking-Prokhorov.

nodes.name: Artin stack of finite type
nodes.statement: By Hilbert scheme argument, the stack ${\mathfrak{DP}_6}$ is an Artin stack of finite type.
nodes.statement_short: Artin stack of finite type
nodes.section: B Moduli stack of sextic du Val del Pezzo surfaces

nodes.name: Non-separatedness of the moduli stack
nodes.statement: The stack ${\mathfrak{DP}_6}$ is not separated --- one can construct two du Val families ${\mathscr{X}} \to {\mathbb{A}}^1$ and~${\mathscr{X}}' \to {\mathbb{A}}^1$ that are isomorphic over ${\mathbb{A}}^1 \setminus \{0\}$, but differ by a small birational transformation over the whole base. The simplest example is to consider the blowup ${\widehat{{\mathscr{X}}}} = \mathrm{Bl}_{{\mathscr{Y}}}({\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{A}}^1) \to {\mathbb{A}}^1$, where ${\mathscr{Y}} = \Big(\{(1,0,0)\} \times {\mathbb{A}}^1\Big) \sqcup \Big(\{(0,1,0)\} \times {\mathbb{A}}^1\Big) \sqcup \Big\{ ((1,1,t),t) \mid t \in {\mathbb{A}}^1 \Big\}$, and define ${\mathscr{X}} \to {\mathbb{A}}^1$ as the family of relative anticanonical models of ${\widehat{{\mathscr{X}}}}$. Then ${\mathscr{X}} \to {\mathbb{A}}^1$ is smooth over~${\mathbb{A}}^1 \times \{0\}$ and degenerates to a singular del Pezzo surface (of type 1) at point $t = 0$. On the other hand, the family ${\mathscr{X}} \times_{{\mathbb{A}}^1} ({\mathbb{A}}^1 \setminus \{0\}) \to {\mathbb{A}}^1 \setminus \{0\}$ is isomorphic to the trivial family, hence can be extended to a trivial family ${\mathscr{X}}' \to {\mathbb{A}}^1$. Thus, the families~${\mathscr{X}}$ and ${\mathscr{X}}'$ are isomorphic over ${\mathbb{A}}^1 \setminus \{0\}$, but have different fibers over $0$.
nodes.section: B Moduli stack of sextic du Val del Pezzo surfaces
nodes.statement_short: The stack is not separated: a blowup family degenerating to a type 1 surface agrees off the origin with a trivial family.

nodes.name: Variety $\mathbb{X}_2 = \mathbb{P}(W_1)\times\mathbb{P}(W_2)$
nodes.statement: Denote by $W_1$ and $W_2$ two three-dimensional vector spaces, consider the product \begin{equation*} {\mathbb{X}}_2 := {\mathbb{P}}(W_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2), \end{equation*} its Segre embedding ${\mathbb{X}}_2 \hookrightarrow {\mathbb{P}}(W_1 \otimes W_2) =: {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}})$, and the standard exceptional collection on ${{\mathbb{X}}_2}$: \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{X}}_2}) = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}, {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,2), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,2), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2) \rangle. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Mutated exceptional collection on $\mathbb{X}_2$
nodes.statement: An easy computation shows that the result is the following exceptional collection \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{X}}_2}) = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,-1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(-1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}, {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,2), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2) \rangle. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Symmetric rectangular Lefschetz decomposition of $\mathbb{X}_2$
nodes.statement: Clearly, this is a rectangular Lefschetz collection with respect to ${\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1)$ with three blocks equal to \begin{equation} {\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}^{\rm{sym}} = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,-1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(-1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2} \rangle. \end{equation}

nodes.name: First Lefschetz block for $\mathbb{X}_2$
nodes.statement: {\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}^{\rm{sym}} = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,-1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(-1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2} \rangle.
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Bundle $\mathscr{W}_2$ presenting $\mathbb{X}_2$ as a projectivization
nodes.statement: Indeed, the scheme~${{\mathbb{X}}_2}$ can be considered as a projectivization of a vector bundle \begin{equation*} {{\mathbb{X}}_2} \cong {\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}({\mathscr{W}}_2), \qquad {\mathscr{W}}_2 := W_2\otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1) \subset {\mathbb{W}} \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Linear HPD for $\mathbb{X}_2$ (first block $\mathbf{D}(\mathbb{P}(W_1))$)
nodes.statement: Consequently, by~\cite[Corollary~8.3]{kuznetsov2007hpd} the homological projectively dual of ${{\mathbb{X}}_2}$ with respect to the Lefschetz decomposition with the first block ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(W_1))$ is \begin{equation} {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} := {\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}({\mathscr{W}}_2^\perp), \end{equation} where ${\mathscr{W}}_2^\perp := \mathrm{Ker}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)} \to {\mathscr{W}}_2^\vee) \cong W_2^\vee \otimes \Omega_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1)$ is a rank 6 vector bundle on~${\mathbb{P}}(W_1)$.
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.statement_short: By linear HPD, the dual of $\mathbb{X}_2$ for the standard Lefschetz decomposition is $\mathbb{Y}_2 = \mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}(W_1)}(\mathscr{W}_2^\perp)$.

nodes.name: Definition of $\mathbb{Y}_2$
nodes.statement: {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} := {\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}({\mathscr{W}}_2^\perp),

nodes.statement: The variety ${{\mathbb{Y}}_2}$ is homologically projectively dual to the variety ${{\mathbb{X}}_2}$ with respect to the Lefschetz decomposition of ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{X}}_2)$ with first block~\eqref{eq:xx3-lefschetz}.
