nodes.name: Proof of Theorem C.1
nodes.statement: Let ${{\mathscr{X}}_2} \subset {{\mathbb{X}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)$ be the universal hyperplane section of ${{\mathbb{X}}_2}$. By~\cite[Theorem~8.2]{kuznetsov2007hpd}, there is a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(W_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(W_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2) \rangle, \end{equation} where the morphisms $i$ and $\phi$ are defined by the Cartesian diagram \begin{equation} \vcenter{\xymatrix{ {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2) \ar[r]^-i \ar[d]_\phi & {{\mathscr{X}}_2} \ar[d]^{p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}} \\ {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \ar[r]^-{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}} & {\mathbb{P}}(W_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee) \ar[r]^-{p_2} & {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee) }} \end{equation} and the map $p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}$ is induced by the embedding ${\mathscr{W}}_2^\perp \hookrightarrow {\mathbb{W}}^\vee \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}$. We modify~\eqref{eq:dbxx3-1} by a sequence of mutations to change it to the form we need. First, using the standard exceptional collection ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(W_1)) = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}, {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1) \rangle$, decomposition \eqref{eq:dbxx3-1} can be rewritten as \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2})), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,2), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(3,2) \rangle. \end{multline*} Mutating the last component to the far left and taking into account that $\omega_{{\mathscr{X}}_2} \cong {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(-2,-2)$ up to a line bundle pulled back from ${\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)$, we obtain a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,0), i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2})), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,2), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2) \rangle. \end{multline*} Next, mutating the second component one step to the left, we get \begin{multline} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2}) = \langle \Phi({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2})), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,0), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,2), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2) \rangle. \end{multline} where $\Phi = {\mathbb{L}}_{{\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,0)} \circ i_* \circ \phi^* \colon {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2}) \to {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2})$. This almost proves the result. The only small thing left is to show that the functor $\Phi$ is a Fourier--Mukai functor whose kernel is supported on the fiber product ${{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_2}$. For this we note that by~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx3} the functor $i_* \circ \phi^*$ is a Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel $j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2)}$, where $j \colon {\mathbb{Y}}_2 \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2) \to {\mathbb{Y}}_2 \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {\mathscr{X}}_2$ is the embedding induced by the commutative square~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx3}. Moreover, using notation from the diagram~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx3}, the projection functor onto ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,0)$ is given by \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{F}} \mapsto p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*(p_2^*p_{2*}(p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2*}{\mathscr{F}} \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1)), \end{equation*} and its composition with $i_* \circ \phi^*$ is given by \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{F}} \mapsto p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*(p_2^*p_{2*}(p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2*}{\mathscr{F}} \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1)). \end{equation*} In other words, this composition is a Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel $p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1))$ on ${\mathbb{Y}}_2 \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {\mathscr{X}}_2$. Therefore, the functor $\Phi$ fits into a distinguished triangle \begin{equation*} \Phi_{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1))} \to \Phi_{j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2)}} \to \Phi. \end{equation*} It follows from~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx3} that \begin{equation*} j^*(p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1))) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2)}, \end{equation*} hence by~\cite{anno2012adjunction} the above triangle of functors is induced by (a rotation of the twist of) the triangle associated with the standard exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2), {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_2}} \to {\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_2}} \to j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2)} \to 0. \end{equation*} It finally proves, that up to an irrelevant shift, the functor $\Phi$ is indeed a Fourier--Mukai functor with the kernel \begin{equation} {\mathbb{E}}_2 := {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2), {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_2}} \otimes (p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1))) \in {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {\mathscr{X}}_2), \end{equation} and thus completes the proof of the theorem.
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.statement_short: Start from the linear HPD decomposition of the universal hyperplane section and mutate it into the form required by the symmetric Lefschetz decomposition; then identify the resulting functor as Fourier-Mukai with kernel a twisted ideal sheaf.

nodes.name: Linear HPD decomposition (cited)
nodes.statement: Let ${{\mathscr{X}}_2} \subset {{\mathbb{X}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)$ be the universal hyperplane section of ${{\mathbb{X}}_2}$. By~\cite[Theorem~8.2]{kuznetsov2007hpd}, there is a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(W_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(W_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2) \rangle, \end{equation} where the morphisms $i$ and $\phi$ are defined by the Cartesian diagram \begin{equation} \vcenter{\xymatrix{ {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2) \ar[r]^-i \ar[d]_\phi & {{\mathscr{X}}_2} \ar[d]^{p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}} \\ {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \ar[r]^-{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}} & {\mathbb{P}}(W_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee) \ar[r]^-{p_2} & {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee) }} \end{equation} and the map $p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}$ is induced by the embedding ${\mathscr{W}}_2^\perp \hookrightarrow {\mathbb{W}}^\vee \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Linear HPD decomposition (cited)
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Linear HPD decomposition of the universal hyperplane section
nodes.statement: {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(W_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(W_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2) \rangle,
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.label: eq:dbxx3-1

nodes.name: Cartesian diagram for i and phi
nodes.statement: \vcenter{\xymatrix{ {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2) \ar[r]^-i \ar[d]_\phi & {{\mathscr{X}}_2} \ar[d]^{p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}} \\ {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \ar[r]^-{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}} & {\mathbb{P}}(W_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee) \ar[r]^-{p_2} & {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee) }}
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.label: diagram:yy-cx3

nodes.name: Plan: mutate
nodes.statement: We modify~\eqref{eq:dbxx3-1} by a sequence of mutations to change it to the form we need.
nodes.statement_short: Plan: mutate
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Rewrite using Beilinson collection
nodes.statement: First, using the standard exceptional collection ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(W_1)) = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}, {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1) \rangle$, decomposition \eqref{eq:dbxx3-1} can be rewritten as \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2})), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,2), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(3,2) \rangle. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite using Beilinson collection
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Mutate last component left via canonical class
nodes.statement: Mutating the last component to the far left and taking into account that $\omega_{{\mathscr{X}}_2} \cong {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(-2,-2)$ up to a line bundle pulled back from ${\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)$, we obtain a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,0), i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2})), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,2), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2) \rangle. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Mutate last component left via canonical class
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Mutate to obtain Phi
nodes.statement: Next, mutating the second component one step to the left, we get \begin{multline} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2}) = \langle \Phi({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2})), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,0), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,2), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2) \rangle. \end{multline} where $\Phi = {\mathbb{L}}_{{\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,0)} \circ i_* \circ \phi^* \colon {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2}) \to {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2})$.
nodes.statement_short: Mutate to obtain Phi
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Mutated decomposition with functor Phi
nodes.statement: {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_2}) = \langle \Phi({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2})), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,0), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(0,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,2), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(2,2) \rangle.
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.label: eq:dbxx3-2

nodes.name: Remains: Phi is Fourier-Mukai with the right support
nodes.statement: This almost proves the result. The only small thing left is to show that the functor $\Phi$ is a Fourier--Mukai functor whose kernel is supported on the fiber product ${{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Remains: Phi is Fourier-Mukai with the right support
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: i_* phi^* is Fourier-Mukai
nodes.statement: For this we note that by~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx3} the functor $i_* \circ \phi^*$ is a Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel $j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2)}$, where $j \colon {\mathbb{Y}}_2 \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2) \to {\mathbb{Y}}_2 \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {\mathscr{X}}_2$ is the embedding induced by the commutative square~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx3}.
nodes.statement_short: i_* phi^* is Fourier-Mukai
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Projection functor composition has an explicit kernel
nodes.statement: Moreover, using notation from the diagram~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx3}, the projection functor onto ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_2}(1,0)$ is given by \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{F}} \mapsto p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*(p_2^*p_{2*}(p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2*}{\mathscr{F}} \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1)), \end{equation*} and its composition with $i_* \circ \phi^*$ is given by \begin{equation*} {\mathscr{F}} \mapsto p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*(p_2^*p_{2*}(p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2*}{\mathscr{F}} \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1)). \end{equation*} In other words, this composition is a Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel $p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1))$ on ${\mathbb{Y}}_2 \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {\mathscr{X}}_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Projection functor composition has an explicit kernel
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Triangle of functors
nodes.statement: Therefore, the functor $\Phi$ fits into a distinguished triangle \begin{equation*} \Phi_{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1))} \to \Phi_{j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2)}} \to \Phi. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Triangle of functors
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Triangle comes from the ideal sheaf sequence
nodes.statement: It follows from~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx3} that \begin{equation*} j^*(p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1))) \cong {\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2)}, \end{equation*} hence by~\cite{anno2012adjunction} the above triangle of functors is induced by (a rotation of the twist of) the triangle associated with the standard exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2), {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_2}} \to {\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_2}} \to j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2)} \to 0. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Triangle comes from the ideal sheaf sequence
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Phi has kernel E_2
nodes.statement: It finally proves, that up to an irrelevant shift, the functor $\Phi$ is indeed a Fourier--Mukai functor with the kernel \begin{equation} {\mathbb{E}}_2 := {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2), {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_2}} \otimes (p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1))) \in {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {\mathscr{X}}_2), \end{equation} and thus completes the proof of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Phi has kernel E_2
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: HPD kernel $\mathbb{E}_2$
nodes.statement: {\mathbb{E}}_2 := {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times {\mathbb{P}}(W_2), {{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_2}} \otimes (p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_2}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_1)}(1))) \in {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_2} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)} {\mathscr{X}}_2),
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.label: eq:hpd-kernel-xx3

nodes.name: Two geometric models $\mathbb{Y}_2$, $\mathbb{Y}_2'$
nodes.statement: We could, of course, exchange the role of $W_1$ and $W_2$ in the construction. Then we would get a slightly different homological projectively dual variety as the result, that is \begin{equation*} {\mathbb{Y}}_2' = {\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_2)}(W_1^\vee \otimes \Omega_{{\mathbb{P}}(W_2)}(1)). \end{equation*} Note that the natural maps ${\mathbb{Y}}_2 \to {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)$ and ${\mathbb{Y}}_2' \to {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee)$ are birational onto the same discriminant cubic hypersurface ${\mathscr{D}}_{W_1,W_2} \subset {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{W}}^\vee) = {\mathbb{P}}(W_1^\vee \otimes W_2^\vee)$ and provide two small resolutions of singularities of~${\mathscr{D}}_{W_1,W_2}$, related to each other by a flop, identifying their derived categories. So, the homological projectively dual of ${\mathbb{X}}_2$ as a category is unambiguously defined, but has two different geometric models~${\mathbb{Y}}_2$ and~${\mathbb{Y}}_2'$, breaking down its inner symmetry.
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.statement_short: Exchanging the factors gives a flop-related second small resolution of the discriminant cubic, a second geometric model of the same HPD category.

nodes.name: Fl(1,2;3) is a smooth hyperplane section
nodes.statement: Note that $\mathrm{Fl}(W)$ is a smooth hyperplane section of ${\mathbb{P}}(W) \times {\mathbb{P}}(W^\vee)$ corresponding to the natural bilinear pairing $b_0$ between $W$ and~$W^\vee$.
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: Exceptional collection on $\mathrm{Fl}(W)$ via HPD
nodes.statement: Since~$b_0$ is nondegenerate, it does not lie in the image ${\mathscr{D}}_{W,W^\vee}$ of ${\mathbb{Y}}_2$ in ${\mathbb{P}}(W \otimes W^\vee)$, hence by homological projective duality \cite[Theorem~6.3]{kuznetsov2007hpd} we obtain a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}(\mathrm{Fl}(W)) = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}(0,-1), {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}(-1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}, {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}(1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}(0,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}(1,1) \rangle. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.statement_short: Since the pairing is nondegenerate, HPD gives a six-term exceptional collection on Fl(W).

nodes.name: Lefschetz decomposition of $\mathrm{Fl}(W)$
nodes.statement: Clearly, this is a Lefschetz collection with respect to ${\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}(1,1)$ with two blocks equal to \begin{equation} {\mathcal{A}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}^{\rm{sym}} = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}(0,-1), {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}(-1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)} \rangle. \end{equation}
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$

nodes.name: First Lefschetz block for $\mathrm{Fl}(W)$
nodes.statement: {\mathcal{A}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}^{\rm{sym}} = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}(0,-1), {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)}(-1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{\mathrm{Fl}(W)} \rangle.
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.label: eq:flw-lefschetz

nodes.name: HPD for the flag variety $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.statement: The variety ${{\mathbb{Y}}_2}$ defined by~\eqref{eq:def-yy2} is homological projectively dual to the flag variety $\mathrm{Fl}(W)$ with respect to the Lefschetz decomposition of ${\mathbf{D}}(\mathrm{Fl}(W))$ with first block~\eqref{eq:flw-lefschetz}.
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.statement_short: $\mathbb{Y}_2$ is HP dual to Fl(1,2;3) with respect to the symmetric Lefschetz decomposition.
conclusions: The variety ${{\mathbb{Y}}_2}$ defined by~\eqref{eq:def-yy2} is homological projectively dual to the flag variety $\mathrm{Fl}(W)$ with respect to the Lefschetz decomposition of ${\mathbf{D}}(\mathrm{Fl}(W))$ with first block~\eqref{eq:flw-lefschetz}.
nodes.label: corollary:hpd-fl3

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary C.3
nodes.statement: Follows from Theorem~\ref{theorem:hpd-p2p2} by~\cite[Theorem~3.4]{carocci2015homological}. (see also~\cite[Proposition~A.10]{kuznetsov2018cones}).
nodes.section: C Homological projective duality for ${\mathbb{P}}^2 \times {\mathbb{P}}^2$ and $\mathrm{Fl}(1,2;3)$
nodes.statement_short: Theorem C.1 plus the Carocci-Turcinovic result on HPD for linear systems with base locus.

nodes.name: Variety $\mathbb{X}_3 = (\mathbb{P}^1)^3$
nodes.statement: Denote by $V_1$, $V_2$, and $V_3$ three two-dimensional vector spaces, consider the product \begin{equation*} {{\mathbb{X}}_3} := {\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3), \end{equation*} its Segre embedding ${\mathbb{X}}_3 \hookrightarrow {\mathbb{P}}(V_1 \otimes V_2 \otimes V_3) =: {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}})$, and the standard exceptional collection on ${{\mathbb{X}}_3}$: \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{X}}_3}) = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}, {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,0,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(0,1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(0,0,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,0,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(0,1,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1) \rangle. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Mutated exceptional collection on $\mathbb{X}_3$
nodes.statement: An easy computation shows that what we get is an exceptional collection \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{X}}_3}) = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}, {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,0,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(0,1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(0,0,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,2) \rangle. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Symmetric rectangular Lefschetz decomposition of $\mathbb{X}_3$
nodes.statement: Clearly, this is a rectangular Lefschetz collection with respect to ${\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1)$ with two blocks equal to \begin{equation} {\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}^{\rm{sym}} = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}, {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,0,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(0,1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(0,0,1) \rangle. \end{equation}

nodes.name: First Lefschetz block for $\mathbb{X}_3$
nodes.statement: {\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}^{\rm{sym}} = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}, {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,0,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(0,1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(0,0,1) \rangle.
nodes.label: eq:xx-lefschetz

nodes.name: Bundle $\mathscr{V}_3$ presenting $\mathbb{X}_3$ as a projectivization
nodes.statement: Again, the scheme ${\mathbb{X}}_3$ can be represented as a projectivization of a vector bundle \begin{equation*} {{\mathbb{X}}_3} \cong {\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}({\mathscr{V}}_3), \qquad {\mathscr{V}}_3 := V_3\otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(-1,-1) \subset {\mathbb{V}} \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Linear HPD for $\mathbb{X}_3$ (first block $\mathbf{D}(\mathbb{P}(V_1)\times\mathbb{P}(V_2))$)
nodes.statement: Consequently, by~\cite[Corollary~8.3]{kuznetsov2007hpd} the homological projectively dual of ${{\mathbb{X}}_3}$ with respect to the Lefschetz decomposition with the first block ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2))$ is \begin{equation} {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} := {\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}({\mathscr{V}}_3^\perp), \end{equation} where ${\mathscr{V}}_3^\perp := \mathrm{Ker}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)} \to {\mathscr{V}}_3^\vee) \cong V_3^\vee \otimes \Omega_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1 \otimes V_2)}(1) \vert_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}$ is a rank 6 vector bundle on~${\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: By linear HPD, the dual of $\mathbb{X}_3$ for the Lefschetz decomposition with first block $\mathbf{D}(\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1)$ is $\mathbb{Y}_3$.

nodes.name: Definition of $\mathbb{Y}_3$
nodes.statement: {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} := {\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}({\mathscr{V}}_3^\perp),
nodes.label: eq:def-yy3

nodes.name: Symmetric HPD for $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$
nodes.statement: The variety ${{\mathbb{Y}}_3}$ is homologically projectively dual to the variety ${{\mathbb{X}}_3}$ with respect to the Lefschetz decomposition of ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{X}}_3)$ with first block~\eqref{eq:xx-lefschetz}.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathbb{Y}_3$ is HP dual to $(\mathbb{P}^1)^3$ for the symmetric Lefschetz decomposition with first block (eq:xx-lefschetz).
conclusions: The variety ${{\mathbb{Y}}_3}$ is homologically projectively dual to the variety ${{\mathbb{X}}_3}$ with respect to the Lefschetz decomposition of ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{X}}_3)$ with first block~\eqref{eq:xx-lefschetz}.
nodes.label: theorem:hpd-p1p1p1

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem D.1
nodes.statement: Let ${{\mathscr{X}}_3} \subset {{\mathbb{X}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$ be the universal hyperplane section of ${{\mathbb{X}}_3}$. By~\cite[Theorem~8.2]{kuznetsov2007hpd}, there is a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1) \rangle, \end{equation} where the morphisms $i$ and $\phi$ are defined by the commutative diagram \begin{equation} \vcenter{\xymatrix{ {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3) \ar[r]^-i \ar[d]_\phi & {{\mathscr{X}}_3} \ar[d]^{p_{{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \\ {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \ar[r]^-{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}} & {\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee) \ar[r] & {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee) }} \end{equation} and the map $p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}$ is induced by the embedding ${\mathscr{V}}_3^\perp \hookrightarrow {\mathbb{V}}^\vee \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}$. We modify~\eqref{eq:dbxx1} by a sequence of mutations to change it to the form we need. First, using the standard exceptional collection \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)) = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}, {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(0,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1) \rangle \end{equation*} in ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2))$, we rewrite \eqref{eq:dbxx1} as \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,2,1) \rangle. \end{multline*} Mutating the last component to the far left, and taking into account that $\omega_{{\mathscr{X}}_3} \cong {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(-1,-1,-1)$ up to a line bundle pulled back from ${\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$, we get a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,0), i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1) \rangle. \end{multline*} Next, mutating the second component to the left, we get \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle \Phi({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,0), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1) \rangle. \end{multline*} where $\Phi = {\mathbb{L}}_{{\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,0)} \circ i_* \circ \phi^* \colon {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3}) \to {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3})$. Finally, mutating the second component to the far right and using the pullback of the standard exact sequence $0 \to {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_3)} \to V_3 \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_3)}(1) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_3)}(2) \to 0$, we obtain \begin{multline} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle \Phi({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,2) \rangle. \end{multline} As before, this almost proves the result. The only small thing left is to show that the functor $\Phi$ is a Fourier--Mukai functor whose kernel is supported on the fiber product ${{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}$. The same computations as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{theorem:hpd-p2p2} show that the functor~$\Phi$ fits into a distinguished triangle \begin{equation*} \Phi_{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(-1,-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1))} \to \Phi_{j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)}} \to \Phi, \end{equation*} with notation introduced in~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx}. Again, it follows that this triangle is associated (up to a twist and a rotation) with the standard exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3), {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \to {\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \to j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)} \to 0, \end{equation*} hence the functor $\Phi$ is indeed a Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel \begin{equation} {\mathbb{E}}_3 := {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3), {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \otimes (p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(-1,-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1))) \end{equation} and thus completes the proof of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: As for Theorem C.1: mutate the linear HPD decomposition of the universal hyperplane section into the symmetric form and identify the functor as Fourier-Mukai with a twisted ideal-sheaf kernel.

nodes.name: Linear HPD decomposition (cited)
nodes.statement: Let ${{\mathscr{X}}_3} \subset {{\mathbb{X}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$ be the universal hyperplane section of ${{\mathbb{X}}_3}$. By~\cite[Theorem~8.2]{kuznetsov2007hpd}, there is a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{equation} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1) \rangle, \end{equation} where the morphisms $i$ and $\phi$ are defined by the commutative diagram \begin{equation} \vcenter{\xymatrix{ {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3) \ar[r]^-i \ar[d]_\phi & {{\mathscr{X}}_3} \ar[d]^{p_{{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \\ {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \ar[r]^-{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}} & {\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee) \ar[r] & {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee) }} \end{equation} and the map $p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}$ is induced by the embedding ${\mathscr{V}}_3^\perp \hookrightarrow {\mathbb{V}}^\vee \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Linear HPD decomposition (cited)

nodes.name: Linear HPD decomposition for X_3
nodes.statement: {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1) \rangle,
nodes.label: eq:dbxx1

nodes.name: Diagram for i and phi (X_3)
nodes.statement: \vcenter{\xymatrix{ {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3) \ar[r]^-i \ar[d]_\phi & {{\mathscr{X}}_3} \ar[d]^{p_{{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \\ {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \ar[r]^-{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}} & {\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2) \times {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee) \ar[r] & {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee) }}
nodes.label: diagram:yy-cx

nodes.name: Plan: mutate
nodes.statement: We modify~\eqref{eq:dbxx1} by a sequence of mutations to change it to the form we need.
nodes.statement_short: Plan: mutate

nodes.name: Rewrite using the exceptional collection on P^1 x P^1
nodes.statement: First, using the standard exceptional collection \begin{equation*} {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)) = \langle {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}, {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,0), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(0,1), {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1) \rangle \end{equation*} in ${\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2))$, we rewrite \eqref{eq:dbxx1} as \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,2,1) \rangle. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite using the exceptional collection on P^1 x P^1

nodes.name: Mutate last component left
nodes.statement: Mutating the last component to the far left, and taking into account that $\omega_{{\mathscr{X}}_3} \cong {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(-1,-1,-1)$ up to a line bundle pulled back from ${\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$, we get a semiorthogonal decomposition \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,0), i_*\phi^*({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1) \rangle. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Mutate last component left

nodes.name: Mutate to obtain Phi
nodes.statement: Next, mutating the second component to the left, we get \begin{multline*} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle \Phi({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,0), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1) \rangle. \end{multline*} where $\Phi = {\mathbb{L}}_{{\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,0)} \circ i_* \circ \phi^* \colon {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3}) \to {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3})$.
nodes.statement_short: Mutate to obtain Phi

nodes.name: Mutate to (eq:dbxx6)
nodes.statement: Finally, mutating the second component to the far right and using the pullback of the standard exact sequence $0 \to {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_3)} \to V_3 \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_3)}(1) \to {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_3)}(2) \to 0$, we obtain \begin{multline} {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle \Phi({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,2) \rangle. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Mutate to (eq:dbxx6)

nodes.name: Final mutated decomposition for X_3
nodes.statement: {\mathbf{D}}({{\mathscr{X}}_3}) = \langle \Phi({\mathbf{D}}({{\mathbb{Y}}_3})), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,1), \\ {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(2,1,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,2,1), {\mathbf{D}}({\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)) \otimes {\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{X}}_3}(1,1,2) \rangle.
nodes.label: eq:dbxx6

nodes.name: Remains: Phi is Fourier-Mukai
nodes.statement: As before, this almost proves the result. The only small thing left is to show that the functor $\Phi$ is a Fourier--Mukai functor whose kernel is supported on the fiber product ${{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}$.
nodes.statement_short: Remains: Phi is Fourier-Mukai

nodes.name: Triangle of functors as in Theorem C.1
nodes.statement: The same computations as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{theorem:hpd-p2p2} show that the functor~$\Phi$ fits into a distinguished triangle \begin{equation*} \Phi_{p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(-1,-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1))} \to \Phi_{j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)}} \to \Phi, \end{equation*} with notation introduced in~\eqref{diagram:yy-cx}.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle of functors as in Theorem C.1

nodes.name: Phi has kernel E_3
nodes.statement: Again, it follows that this triangle is associated (up to a twist and a rotation) with the standard exact sequence \begin{equation*} 0 \to {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3), {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \to {\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \to j_*{\mathscr{O}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3)} \to 0, \end{equation*} hence the functor $\Phi$ is indeed a Fourier--Mukai functor with kernel \begin{equation} {\mathbb{E}}_3 := {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3), {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \otimes (p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(-1,-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1))) \end{equation} and thus completes the proof of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Phi has kernel E_3

nodes.name: HPD kernel $\mathbb{E}_3$
nodes.statement: {\mathbb{E}}_3 := {\mathscr{I}}_{{{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_3), {{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \times_{{\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)} {{\mathscr{X}}_3}} \otimes (p_{{\mathbb{Y}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(-1,-1)) \boxtimes p_{{\mathscr{X}}_3}^*({\mathscr{O}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_1) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_2)}(1,1)))
nodes.label: eq:hpd-kernel-xxx3

nodes.name: Fibers of $\mathbb{Y}_3 \to \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{V}^\vee)$
nodes.statement: The natural map ${{\mathbb{Y}}_3} \to {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$ is generically finite of degree 2, and its branch divisor is the Cayley quartic $\overline{\mathrm{O}}_6$ (see Section~\ref{subsection:p1p1p1}). Moreover, the fiber of this morphism is isomorphic to~${\mathbb{P}}^1$ over~${\mathrm{O}}_4$, and to a reducible conic over~${\mathrm{O}}_3$. In particular, ${{\mathbb{Y}}_3}$ provides a small resolution of singularities of the double cover ${\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}$ of~${\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$ branched over~$\overline{\mathrm{O}}_6$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathbb{Y}_3$ is a small resolution of the double cover branched over the Cayley quartic, with fibers $\mathbb{P}^1$ over $O_4$ and conics over $O_3$.
nodes.label: remark:fibers-resolution-dvvv

nodes.name: Six geometric models $\mathbb{Y}_3^\sigma$
nodes.statement: We could, of course, exchange the role of $V_i$ in the construction. Then we would get a slightly different homological projectively dual variety as the result, that is for each permutation ${\sigma} \in {\mathfrak{S}}_3$ we would get \begin{equation*} {\mathbb{Y}}_3^{\sigma} = {\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_{{\sigma}(1)}) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_{{\sigma}(2)})} \Big(V_{{\sigma}(3)}^\vee \otimes \Omega_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_{{\sigma}(1)} \otimes V_{{\sigma}(2)})}(1)\vert_{{\mathbb{P}}(V_{{\sigma}(1)}) \times {\mathbb{P}}(V_{{\sigma}(2)})}\Big). \end{equation*} Note that for each ${\sigma}$ the natural map ${\mathbb{Y}}_3^{\sigma} \to {\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$ factors through a birational morphism onto the double cover ${\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}$ of~${\mathbb{P}}({\mathbb{V}}^\vee)$ branched over $\overline{\mathrm{O}}_6$. They provide six small resolutions of singularities of~${\mathscr{D}}_{V_1,V_2,V_3}$, related to each other by flops, identifying their derived categories. So, the homological projectively dual of~${\mathbb{X}}_3$ as a category is unambiguously defined, but has six different geometric models~${\mathbb{Y}}_3^{\sigma}$, ${\sigma} \in {\mathfrak{S}}_3$, breaking down its inner symmetry.
nodes.statement_short: Permuting the factors gives six flop-related small resolutions of the double cover, models of the same HPD category.
